title: Senior Software Engineer - Fintech
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Us</h3> <p>At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><h3>About the Role</h3> <p>Cloudflare’s Billing Engineering team builds and operates the systems responsible for usage metering, aggregation, subscriptions, invoicing, payments, and revenue recognition. These systems power billions in revenue and support millions of customers across Cloudflare’s product portfolio.</p> <p>We are rebuilding key parts of our billing platform to scale with products including AI, Zero Trust, Workers, Bot Management, and DDoS Protection. As a Senior Software Engineer on the Fintech team, you will design reliable financial infrastructure, lead projects from requirements through production, and help ensure billing remains accurate as Cloudflare grows.</p> <h3>Responsibilities</h3> <p><strong>Build Billing Systems:</strong> Design, develop, and operate transactional microservices supporting metering, subscriptions, invoicing, payments, and financial workflows.</p> <p><strong>Own Projects End to End:</strong> Drive initiatives from requirements and technical design through implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing operation.</p> <p><strong>Ensure Accuracy and Reliability:</strong> Build fault-tolerant systems that safely handle retries, failures, concurrency, and high transaction volumes while preserving financial correctness.</p> <p><strong>Maintain Operational Excellence:</strong> Monitor production services, investigate billing issues, improve observability, and address the underlying causes of recurring incidents.</p> <p><strong>Shape Technical Direction:</strong> Participate in architecture reviews, make pragmatic technical trade-offs, and help improve engineering standards across the billing platform.</p> <p><strong>Collaborate Cross-Functionally:</strong> Work with Product, Finance, Accounting, Support, and other engineering teams to turn complex business requirements into maintainable solutions.</p> <h3>Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience</h3> <p>- Five or more years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience.</p> <p>- Experience building and operating distributed systems or backend services in production.</p> <p>- Proficiency in Go or another modern programming language, with an interest in working extensively with Go.</p> <p>- Strong understanding of RESTful APIs, service security, and API standards such as OpenAPI, OAuth, or JWT.</p> <p>- Working knowledge of SQL, data modeling, and relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.</p> <p>- Experience designing secure, highly available microservices in Linux or Unix environments.</p> <p>- Familiarity with event-driven architectures and asynchronous processing.</p> <p>- Strong troubleshooting, communication, and project ownership skills.</p> <h3>Bonus Points</h3> <p>- Experience with billing, payments, subscriptions, usage metering, invoicing, financial ledgers, or revenue recognition.</p> <p>- Experience with technologies such as PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Docker, or Temporal.</p> <p>- Familiarity with reconciliation, idempotency, auditability, and financial data integrity.</p> <p>- Experience leading technically complex projects across multiple teams.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>What Makes Cloudflare Special?</h3> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.</span></p> <p><a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/protecting-free-expression-online/"><strong>Project Galileo</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.</span></p> <p><strong><a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/athenian/">Athenian Project</a></strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. title: Senior ERP Engineer - Odoo (d/f/m)
description: Deine Mission As Senior ERP Engineer - Odoo (d/f/m), you shape how our ERP grows. Odoo runs our invoicing, hardware logistics and energy market communication, and over the next year it becomes the source of truth for customer and contract data and takes over electricity billing. You design the data model and module architecture, build integrations with our platform and partners, and hold the quality bar for the team. You do not only ask "How do we build this in Odoo", but also "Should this live in Odoo at all". Deine Verantwortlichkeiten Designing and building custom Odoo modules, from data model to UI Making architecture decisions for a growing ERP, including what belongs in Odoo and what doesn’t Driving the migration of customer, contract and metering processes from HubSpot into Odoo Building and maintaining integrations with our internal platform and external partners in logistics, metering and market communication Shipping features to production independently Setting technical standards for code reviews, automated tests, CI and code quality Reviewing code and pairing with our developers and our external Odoo partner Working closely with Finance and Ops to turn their needs into clear scope and reliable estimates Dein Profil You bring 5+ years of software development , several of them hands-on with Odoo (custom modules, ORM, views, security rules, major version upgrades) You work confidently with Python and PostgreSQL You’ve built ERP integrations (REST APIs, webhooks, batch jobs) that run reliably in production Git, CI and automated tests are part of your daily routine You think in data models and processes , not just in tickets You raise risks early , say clearly when a deadline won’t hold and push back when needed, including with non-technical stakeholders You speak fluent English Unser Offer Real influence on a core system: shape the ERP our whole business runs on Impact on the energy transition: work powers billing, logistics and market communication for smart home energy More room to shape things than at an Odoo agency or in a large corporate Short paths to Finance, Ops and our CTO, no long chains of command Flexibility: work remotely from anywhere in Germany or from our offices in Berlin and Cologne Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Sales & Client Engagement Director (EMEA + DACH)
description: <h2>About us</h2> <p><a href="https://constructorlabs.org/">Constructor Labs</a> is the research arm of Constructor Knowledge, based at Campus Ring 1 in Bremen, Germany. Our work is organized around three units: Knowledge Labs, Cyber Labs and Science Labs. We apply computing, software and robotics research to make scientists, teachers and students more effective, working with institutional partners that include CERN, NUS, Carnegie Mellon and Fraunhofer.</p> <p>Our <a href="https://constructorlabs.org/solutions/edtech/">EdTech practice</a> produces research that runs in production. AI-supported remote proctoring is in use at the Irish Aviation Authority, Princess Nourah University and Saudi Electronic University, and our course delivery platform is used by CERN, EPFL, MariaDB and Acronis. For industry clients, we build tailored BSc, MSc and PhD pipelines, L&D operating models, AI upskilling programmes and customer training systems.</p> <p><strong>Constructor Labs Solutions (CLS)</strong> is our client-facing systems integrator for the education and research sector, launching in September 2026. It brings audit and consultancy, content, platform, talent and R&D services together under a single contract, an offer few providers make to education buyers today. Delivery is orchestrated across several Constructor organizations: CUB, Nexford, Nexademy, EBAC, Constructor Labs and Constructor Tech. Our aim is to become the go-to systems integrator for education in EMEA by 2029.</p> <h2>The role</h2> <p>You will open EMEA markets for Constructor Labs Solutions as a quota-carrying individual contributor. The role rests on an established network among universities, online education providers, EdTech vendors and corporate L&D and research buyers, and on your ability to convert that network into signed engagements.</p> <p>You will work with the marketing and delivery teams to build pipeline, establish the CLS brand and develop a case-study library. Supporting you are a credible research institution, named production references, an existing Constructor and Constructor Tech client base, and delivery capability across five service lines that can be combined into a single proposal.</p> <p>The sales motion is consultative. Engagements typically open with a low-risk paid diagnostic (Technology Landscape Assessment, Curriculum Gap Analysis or Learning Strategy Advisory), which you then convert into a multi-line implementation or managed-service mandate. Initial engagements start at around €150–250K in lifetime value and grow from there. Sales cycles in public higher education run six to twelve months, so you will manage a long-cycle institutional funnel alongside faster corporate L&D deals.</p> <h2>Reporting and scope</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Reports to:</strong> Director of Sales & Marketing, Constructor Labs Solutions (shared with the Constructor Labs GM during Phase 1).</li> <li><strong>Level:</strong> Director, individual contributor. You will join an established sales team.</li> <li><strong>Territory:</strong> EMEA, with initial focus on DACH (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) and the UK and Ireland. Named accounts agreed quarterly.</li> <li><strong>Segments:</strong> traditional and online universities, EdTech providers and platform vendors, corporate L&D and corporate academies, research-intensive organizations, and publicly funded research programmes.</li> <li><strong>Portfolio:</strong> all five CLS service lines, namely Audit & Consultancy, Content, Platform, Talent and R&D Services.</li> </ul> <p>Day-to-day, you will work with the Audit & Consultancy Practice Head on scoping, with Nexademy on content propositions, with Constructor Tech on platform architecture, and with the Labs' principal investigators, who join client conversations to provide subject-matter credibility. Knowing which expert belongs in which conversation is central to the role.</p> <h2>What you will do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Pipeline generation.</strong> Around 70% of your time is spent on outbound activity: your own network, conference presence, sector associations, procurement frameworks and targeted account campaigns, supported by marketing.</li> <li><strong>Reference accounts.</strong> Sign the first reference clients in EMEA and develop each one into a published case study, an active sponsor and a source of introductions.</li> <li><strong>Discovery and scoping.</strong> Map the client's learning or research operating model and quantify the problem in their own measures: cost per course, time to accreditation, completion rates, time-to-hire, research throughput. Shape a diagnostic that leads to a defined follow-on engagement.</li> <li><strong>Conversion to implementation.</strong> Own the transition from paid diagnostic to multi-line mandate, with a target of converting half of all audit engagements.</li> <li><strong>Proposals and bids.</strong> Assemble proposals across the five service lines with the practice heads, price them against the finance model and qualify them against margin floors. Lead RFP and framework responses, including public-sector tenders in Germany and the UK.</li> <li><strong>Stakeholder coverage.</strong> Engage rectors, deans, CIOs, heads of digital learning, procurement, works councils, CLOs, HR directors and research directors. Maintain at least three engaged contacts on every opportunity above €200K.</li> <li><strong>Partner channel.</strong> Recruit and manage regional partners, resellers, agencies and academic networks that extend reach beyond your direct coverage.</li> <li><strong>Quota and forecasting.</strong> You carry an annual new-business quota, with quarterly KPIs covering pipeline coverage, audit conversion, average engagement value and blended margin. title: PhD Position: World Models for Software Architecture Synthesis (Constructor Fabric)
description: <p><strong>Supervisor: </strong>Prof. Dr. Alexander Tormasov<strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>About the Position</strong></p> <p>Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL), in collaboration with Constructor Technology, invites applications for a PhD position in machine learning for software engineering and formal methods, on the Constructor Fabric project.</p> <p>Constructor Fabric turns a company's informal knowledge into production software through a pipeline of composable capability units called <em>gears</em>: requirements → architecture → product fit → framework (G1) → application → runtime. We are building a <strong>World Model</strong> over that pipeline — a model that does not just generate code, but predicts the <em>consequences</em> of an architectural decision: total cost of ownership, unintended side effects, latency and failure behaviour, and whether a proposed composition is even admissible.</p> <p><br>The central object is not a digital twin of the application but its <strong>formal architectural skeleton</strong>: gear contracts (GearSpec), a typed attributed hypergraph of the application (AppGraph), a composition algebra that defines which assemblies are legal, and several semantic projections (types, protocols, resources, security) over which properties are proved, refuted by counterexample, or reported as an explainable <strong>gap</strong>. All of it is written in a <strong>domain-specific language</strong> whose syntax trees and graphs we keep in a projectional editor (JetBrains MPS) — so the DSL is not a convenience layer, it is the thing that defines the model's state space and the boundary of what the model is allowed to propose.</p> <p><strong>What you will work on</strong><br>Depending on your background, one or two of:</p> <ol> <li>Formal skeleton and composition — GearSpec as a contract $(Requires, Provides, State, Effects, Assumptions, Guarantees, Parameters)$; AppGraph as a typed attributed hypergraph; an algebra of assembly (sequential, parallel, feedback, refinement); semantic projections and system-level invariants over trajectories.</li> <li>Architecture synthesis as an inverse problem — given a specification, load and constraints, find the composition of gears that realises it. Constraint solving and MCTS as the baseline; a learned transition/value model for ranking and pruning; LLM proposals treated strictly as candidate hypotheses that a DSL parser, type checker and property checks must then admit or reject.</li> <li>DSL design and language engineering — the gear DSL and its glue layer decide which AppGraphs are expressible at all, and therefore where the search space ends. This thread covers the abstract syntax and static semantics of that DSL; the requirement that an architectural decision be unbypassable by construction (you must not be able to wire authentication around the Auth Resolver); what happens to the language when gear contracts change or a 201st gear is added; projectional representation of graphs with cycles; and the open hypothesis that a specialised G1-DSL is generated together with every G1.</li> <li>Local transition models and pipeline surrogates — fast approximate predictors for single pipeline steps (spec change → code quality, architecture → product fit, app → runtime outcome), with calibrated uncertainty, validated against real telemetry.</li> <li>Data — reconstructing (specification → architecture) pairs from open repositories at scale, plus synthetic project generation from a fixed gear set and DSL grammar to cover rare transitions, gaps and counterexamples.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Profile</strong></p> <ul> <li>MSc (or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, or a mathematical natural science.</li> <li>Coursework in compilers, programming-language theory, language design or model-driven engineering is a strong positive signal, half of this project is deciding what a formal architecture description is allowed to say.</li> <li>Evidence that you finish things: a maintained open-source repository, a peer-reviewed publication, or a strong competition result.</li> <li>Fluent technical English.</li> <li>Most importantly: the habit of stating an assumption explicitly and designing an experiment that could falsify it.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required mathematical background</strong></p> <p><strong><em>Core skills:</em></strong></p> <ul> <li>Probability and statistics. Estimation, Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification and calibration (proper scoring rules, reliability diagrams, ECE), experiment design and significance testing. A prediction we cannot calibrate is not usable here.</li> <li>Linear algebra and multivariate calculus at the level needed to derive, not just call, a training objective: matrix calculus, gradients, stochastic optimisation, conditioning.</li> <li>Discrete mathematics and graph theory. Typed and attributed graphs and hypergraphs, subgraph matching and isomorphism, graph rewriting, reachability, basic complexity classes.</li> <li>Mathematical logic and formal methods. First-order logic, type systems, SAT/SMT, temporal logic (LTL/CTL) and model checking, pre/post-conditions, invariants, refinement.</li> <li>Sequential decision making. MDP/POMDP, dynamic programming, model-based RL, latent state-space (world) models, Monte-Carlo Tree Search.</li> </ul> <p><strong><em>Strong command of at least one, working knowledge of a second:</em></strong></p> <ul> <li>Formal languages, semantics and language engineering — grammars (context-free, attribute and graph grammars), derivation and reachability, parsing; abstract versus concrete syntax; operational and denotational semantics; metamodelling, model-driven engineering, model-to-model transformation, and projectional (structural) editing of the kind JetBrains MPS implements. We are asking for the education, not the tool: you should know why a projectional editor exists, what a metamodel buys you over a text grammar, and how a language evolves without breaking its existing models. Hands-on MPS experience is explicitly not required — we will teach it.</li> <li>Category theory for compositional systems — monoidal and traced monoidal categories, functors as semantic projections, string diagrams, operads. This is the language of our assembly algebra.</li> <li>Causal inference — structural causal models, do-calculus, counterfactuals, identifiability. Required for the "what happens if we replace this technology / move on-premises" class of questions, which similarity search alone cannot answer.</li> <li>Queueing theory and applied stochastic processes — M/M/1 and networks of queues, heavy tails, retries, timeouts, partial failure and reliability models. This is the resource and stochastic projection.</li> <li>Combinatorial optimisation, constraint programming and program synthesis theory — CEGIS, version-space algebras, symmetry breaking, search heuristics.</li> <li>Representation learning theory — VAEs and latent dynamics, GNN expressiveness (Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy), permutation equivariance, embedding migration under a changing vocabulary.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required hands-on programming skills</strong></p> <p>This is an engineering-heavy PhD. We expect code that another person can clone, run and reproduce — not notebooks that worked once.</p> <p><strong><em>Must have:</em></strong></p> <ul> <li>Python (professional level). Type hints, packaging, `pytest`, profiling, `asyncio`, memory-aware data structures. You write unbuffered, logged, restartable long-running jobs by default.</li> <li>Training loops written from scratch, custom datasets and collation, mixed precision, multi-GPU; experiment tracking (W&B or MLflow), configuration management (Hydra), strict seed and artefact reproducibility.</li> <li>Graph machine learning. PyTorch Geometric or DGL — message passing, heterogeneous and typed graphs, graph transformers, handling graphs whose node vocabulary changes between versions.</li> <li>Solvers and verification tooling driven from Python. Z3 or cvc5 hands-on; demonstrated exposure to at least one model checker (TLA+/TLC, SPIN, NuSMV, Alloy) or proof assistant (Lean, Coq, Isabelle).</li> <li>Code as data. AST manipulation, `tree-sitter`, static analysis, dependency and interface graph extraction, large-scale repository mining.</li> <li>Parallel data pipelines. `multiprocessing`, Ray or Dask; checkpointing, heartbeats, cost estimation before launching a run that touches millions of files.</li> <li>LLM engineering. API orchestration, structured and grammar-constrained decoding, evaluation harnesses, token/cost accounting — with the discipline to treat model output as a hypothesis subject to formal checks.</li> <li>Linux, git, code review, shell.</li> </ul> <p><strong><em>Desirable:</em></strong></p> <ul> <li>Language tooling you have actually used: ANTLR, Xtext, Lark, or a parser, type checker or interpreter you wrote yourself. Our internal representation of gear syntax trees and graphs lives in JetBrains MPS — again, we do not ask for MPS experience, only that you are comfortable reading and extending a metamodel; Java/Kotlin literacy helps once you get there.</li> <li>JAX, or compiler / SAT-SMT internals.</li> <li>Infrastructure literacy — Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry/Prometheus — since the resource projection is calibrated against real deployment telemetry.</li> <li>One systems language (Rust, Go or C++) for performance-critical search.</li> <li>Prior experience with production software architecture, or with a brownfield system you had to change without breaking.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Funding</strong></p> <p>The appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:</p> <ul> <li>Monthly stipend of €1,650</li> <li>Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)</li> <li>Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month</li> </ul> <p><strong>Location: </strong>Bremen, Germany</p> <p><strong>Duration: </strong>3 years, full time</p> <p><strong>Start date: </strong> November 2026</p> <p><strong>Application package must include</strong></p> <ul> <li>CV, including publications, code, or research projects.</li> <li>Cover letter (1–2 pages) explaining your motivation, research interests, and fit with the project.</li> <li>A link to code you have written.</li> <li>A one-page research statement picking one open research question from the project and sketching how you would approach it.</li> <li>Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificate and transcripts.</li> <li>Contact information for 2–3 academic referees.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.</strong></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Internship position for World Models for Software Architecture (Constructor Fabric)
description: <p><strong>About the Project</strong></p> <p>Constructor Fabric turns a company's informal knowledge into production software through a pipeline of composable capability units called <em>gears</em>: requirements → architecture → product fit → framework (G1) → application → runtime. We are building a <strong>World Model</strong> over that pipeline — a model that does not just generate code, but predicts the <em>consequences</em> of an architectural decision: total cost of ownership, unintended side effects, latency and failure behaviour, and whether a proposed composition is even admissible.<br>The central object is not a digital twin of the application but its <strong>formal architectural skeleton</strong>: gear contracts (GearSpec), a typed attributed hypergraph of the application (AppGraph), a composition algebra that defines which assemblies are legal, and several semantic projections (types, protocols, resources, security) over which properties are proved, refuted by counterexample, or reported as an explainable <strong>gap</strong>. All of it is written in a <strong>domain-specific language</strong> whose syntax trees and graphs we keep in a projectional editor (JetBrains MPS) — so the DSL is not a convenience layer, it is the thing that defines the model's state space and the boundary of what the model is allowed to propose.</p> <p><strong>Internship Role</strong></p> <p>As a Research Intern (Machine Learning for Software Engineering), you will support the data and modelling work behind the World Model — mining code, building datasets, and running baseline experiments. We are looking for students who are keen to collaborate with industrial companies working with AI, open to out-of-the-box topics, and interested in a long-term collaboration.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Mine open-source repositories and extract architecture, dependency, and interface graphs from code.</li> <li>Help build and clean (specification → architecture) datasets, including synthetic project generation.</li> <li>Implement and evaluate baseline models (heuristic search, graph ML, or LLM generation) for single pipeline steps.</li> <li>Benchmark models against shared datasets and metrics to compare approaches.</li> <li>Build evaluation harnesses and track experiments reproducibly.</li> <li>Assist with documentation and, where relevant, publication activities.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Currently enrolled in a BSc/MSc in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, or similar.</li> <li>Experience with Python and ML frameworks (PyTorch, scikit-learn).</li> <li>Interest in machine learning for code, software engineering, or formal methods.</li> <li>Good English and teamwork skills.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desired Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Predictive models/time-series/etc.</li> <li>LLM tooling.</li> <li>Familiarity with graph machine learning (PyTorch Geometric or DGL).</li> <li>Interest in formal methods, program or static analysis, or working with code structure (e.g. AST manipulation, tree-sitter, or repository mining).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Application Details</strong></p> <p>Please submit:</p> <ul> <li>CV</li> <li>Short motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining your interest and relevant skills</li> <li>Transcript of records (GPA obligatory)</li> </ul> Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer (OpenStack Ironic Specialist)
description: <h2>About Nscale</h2> <p>Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.</p> <p>We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.</p> <h2>About the Role</h2> <p>We’re hiring an <strong><strong class="textBold">Infrastructure Engineer (OpenStack Ironic Specialist)</strong></strong> to design, operate, and continuously improve the bare metal provisioning platforms that underpin Nscale’s infrastructure.</p> <p>This role sits within the <strong><strong class="textBold">Infrastructure Engineering team</strong></strong>, which is responsible for the design, implementation, operation, and ongoing improvement of the infrastructure stack supporting both internal and customer-facing services. You’ll work closely with <strong><strong class="textBold">network, compute, data centre, support, and pre-sales teams</strong></strong>, while also serving as a specialist escalation point for advanced provisioning and hardware issues.</p> <p>This is a high-impact role focused on <strong><strong class="textBold">OpenStack Ironic</strong></strong>, automated hardware lifecycle management, and the reliable operation of large-scale physical infrastructure. You’ll also help connect Nscale to the broader <strong><strong class="textBold">upstream OpenStack community</strong></strong>, ensuring our bare metal platforms evolve in line with real operational needs and industry direction.</p> <h2>What you'll be doing</h2> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">Bare Metal Provisioning & Lifecycle Management</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1"><strong><strong class="textBold">Design</strong></strong> scalable and resilient bare metal provisioning platforms with a strong focus on <strong><strong class="textBold">OpenStack Ironic</strong></strong>.</li> <li value="2"><strong><strong class="textBold">Own</strong></strong> the full lifecycle of physical infrastructure, including discovery, enrolment, provisioning, class="textBold">Automation & Platform Integration</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1"><strong><strong class="textBold">Manage</strong></strong> and improve integrations between <strong><strong class="textBold">Ironic</strong></strong> and related OpenStack services such as <strong><strong class="textBold">Nova, Neutron, Glance, Keystone, and Placement</strong></strong>.</li> <li value="2"><strong><strong class="textBold">Drive</strong></strong> automation for hardware onboarding, firmware and BIOS configuration, deployment workflows, validation, and recovery.</li> <li value="3"><strong><strong class="textBold">Implement</strong></strong> infrastructure automation using <strong><strong class="textBold">infrastructure-as-code</strong></strong> and configuration management approaches.</li> <li value="4"><strong><strong class="textBold">Ensure</strong></strong> provisioning platforms and operational processes align with security, compliance, and operational standards.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">Troubleshooting, Reliability & Operational Support</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1"><strong><strong and you build trusted relationships with stakeholders</li> <li>Advanced SQL (or equivalent)</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of BI tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI, Looker)</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to Business Analytics, Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Actuarial Studies or a related field</li> </ul> <p><strong>Don’t tick every box?</strong> Research shows women often hold back from applying title: Director, Technical Program Management, Networking
description: <h2><strong>About Nscale</strong></h2> <p>Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.</p> <p>We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.</p> <h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2> <p>We're seeking a Director of Technical Program Management – Networking to build and lead the team of Technical Program Managers who deliver Nscale's network infrastructure across Europe. This team sits within our Deployment organisation, a build org that owns every step from hardware arrival on site through to customer acceptance.</p> <p>You'll own the delivery of cluster networking, data centre networking, and WAN programmes across our European sites, leading TPMs who partner with Network Engineering, Data Centre Operations, Supply Chain, and external carriers and vendors. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has delivered networks at hyperscale and knows how to turn complex, multi-site builds into predictable, repeatable execution. The role involves regular travel to our sites and partners.</p> <h2><strong>What You'll be Doing</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Build, lead, and mentor a team of Technical Program Managers covering cluster networking, data centre networking, and WAN delivery across Europe.</li> <li>Own the end-to-end network delivery plan for new GPU cluster builds and expansions, from hardware arrival through installation, validation, and customer acceptance.</li> <li>Set the operating model for network programme delivery: planning standards, milestone gates, risk and dependency management, and reporting.</li> <li>Partner with Network Engineering on design readiness, BOMs, and build sequencing for Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics, front-end networks, and WAN interconnects.</li> <li>Drive alignment across Deployment, Data Centre Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, SRE, and Commercial teams so network delivery never blocks customer handover.</li> <li>Manage strategic relationships with carriers, IXPs, colocation providers, and network hardware vendors.</li> <li>Establish metrics for delivery speed, quality, and predictability, and use them to drive continuous improvement.</li> <li>Communicate status, risks, and trade-offs clearly to executive leadership and customers.</li> <li>Hire top TPM talent in a highly competitive market and grow a high-performing, accountable team culture.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About You</strong></h2> <ul> <li>12+ years of experience in technical programme management, network engineering, or infrastructure delivery, including 5+ years leading TPM or engineering teams.</li> <li>Track record delivering large-scale network infrastructure at a hyperscaler or major network vendor (e.g. Microsoft, AWS, Oracle/OCI, Cisco, or similar).</li> <li>Strong technical grounding in cluster and data centre networking, WAN, and routing (BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics).</li> <li>Experience running multi-site, multi-country builds with complex hardware, vendor, and carrier dependencies.</li> <li>Proven ability to build programme management frameworks that scale with a fast-growing organisation.</li> <li>Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills; comfortable influencing without authority.</li> <li>Willingness to travel regularly across Europe to sites and partners.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience delivering networking for large GPU clusters or AI training environments.</li> <li>Familiarity with HPC network topologies (Fat Tree, Rail) and high-speed optics (400G/800G).</li> <li>Experience with network automation and infrastructure-as-code in a deployment context.</li> <li>PMP, PgMP, or similar certification.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Why this role matters</strong></h2> <p>Every GPU we deploy is only as useful as the network that connects it. This role sets how quickly and reliably Nscale turns hardware into capacity our customers can use, and shapes how network delivery scales as we expand across Europe.</p> <h2><strong>Equal Opportunities Statement</strong></h2> <p>At Nscale, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.</p> <p>If there's anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.</p> <p>The responsibilities outlined in this job description are not exhaustive and are intended to provide a general overview of the position. The employee may be required to perform additional duties, tasks, and responsibilities as assigned by management, consistent with the skills and qualifications required for the role.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>For information on how Nscale handles candidate personal data, please see our Employee & Candidate Privacy Notice: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1QK5Yg04WHD9K9IAtJgQWubJZC9oLvatK/view?usp=sharing" target="_blank" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1QK5Yg04WHD9K9IAtJgQWubJZC9oLvatK/view?usp%3Dsharing&source=gmail&ust=1765375172804000&usg=AOvVaw2Ncte4rmlGl8OKuFuDgDtx">Here.</a><br><br>Nscale does not accept unsolicited candidate submissions from recruitment agencies.<br></em></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Security Operations Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"><strong>Who we are</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 300; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 300; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.</span></p></div><p><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p>As a member of our Security Operations Team, you will collaborate with a global team of engineers to monitor and respond to security events, lead security incidents as Incident Commander, and lead digital forensic investigations in support of Employee Relations, Legal, Compliance, or Information Security cases.</p> <p>Although you will be focused on security incident response, you will also have the opportunity to create and maintain runbooks, and automated workflows, and assist in process refinement and implementation. You will collaborate with a diverse team of engineers, and key stakeholders on security initiatives across the company. Above all, your focus is bringing Security expertise to the table in a collaborative, humble, and practical manner.</p> <p><strong>Location:</strong> This role is open to candidates residing in Netherlands</p> <p><strong>You should apply if:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>You want to impact the industries that run our world:</strong> Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.</li> <li><strong>You thrive the most when solving problems:</strong> Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.</li> <li><strong>You are a natural relationship builder:</strong> Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.</li> <li><strong>You are the architect of your own career:</strong> If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.</li> <li><strong>You want to be with the best: </strong>At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.</li> </ul> <p><strong>In this role, you will: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Monitor security events and provide technical analysis on alerts</li> <li>Lead information security incidents and employee insider investigations by developing the incident response strategy, lead the execution through incident closure, while providing incident updates to key stakeholders throughout the incident</li> <li>Deliver security guidance clearly and concisely for incident response and insider threat initiatives</li> <li>Coordinate the building of services, capabilities, integrations, and implementations of technologies to support security operations, incident response, and insider threat</li> <li>Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices</li> <li>Participate in our on-call rota covering weekends</li> </ul> <p><strong>Minimum requirements for the role:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in Security Incident Response</li> <li>Ability to communicate investigative findings and strategies to technical staff, executive leadership, and legal</li> <li>Ability to build scripts or tools to support Samsara’s investigation processes, with proficiency in Python</li> <li>Mentor and train security operation engineers on data collection, analysis, and reporting technical analysis</li> <li>Practical experience acting as a lead during security incident response, including monitoring and triaging alerts, and coordinating across teams</li> <li>Understanding of analysis and forensics techniques on macOS, Windows, and Linux</li> <li>Experience utilizing SIEM tools to perform log reviews</li> <li>Experience in cloud architecture and security (AWS, GCP) and cloud-based services</li> <li>Participation in an on-call rotation, with the potential to work outside standard business hours, including late evenings, when responding to high-severity incidents as part of our global incident response team.</li> <li>This role will be part of our EMEA so your hours will be aligned to the UK. As an operational time you may be expected to work flexible hours around this to support the load of the team</li> </ul> <p><strong>An ideal candidate also has:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of experience working on insider threat initiatives or employee investigations</li> <li>Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field - or relevant industry experience</li> <li>GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) or similar Certification</li> <li>Familiarity with common security frameworks and standards, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, FedRAMP</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Total Rewards</strong></p> <p>At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description: <p>We are looking for a <strong>Senior Data Platform Engineer</strong> to join the <strong>Data Platform</strong> at Smartly!</p> <p>Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.</p> <p>This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.</p> <p>Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems.</p> <p>This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.</p> <h2>What you will do</h2> <ul> <li>Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.</li> <li>Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.</li> <li>Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.</li> <li>Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.</li> <li>Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.</li> <li>Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.</li> <li>Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.</li> <li>Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.</li> </ul> <h2>What we are looking for</h2> <ul> <li>Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.</li> <li>Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.</li> <li>Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, title: Senior Solutions Architect | Germany | Remote
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. You’ll guide organizations through onboarding, implementation, and expansion by offering white-glove support, best practices, and proven strategies gathered from across our customer base.</p> <p data-start="932" data-end="1337">You’ll operate with one foot in the code and the other in the customer’s world. Whether it’s understanding container orchestration in Kubernetes, fine-tuning Prometheus queries, or clarifying the nuances between logs, metrics, and traces—you’ll bring clarity and confidence to complex technical landscapes. This team is nimble and is the fulcrum to accelerate the delivery of the solution for customers.</li> <li>Be a strong advocate for adherence to standards and best practices.</li> <li>Stay current on Grafana Labs, observability, and related technologies.</li> <li>You'll be a key resource for our Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Support, and Professional Services teams as they look to drive innovation and improvements into future product and offering enhancements.</li> <li>If you enjoy working with customers to help them succeed and thrive on working with leading-edge technologies, this is the role for you.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What Makes You a Great Fit:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Located in the Germany </li> <li>5+ years of experience working on deployment teams, using project management techniques.</li> <li>Direct experience with o11y.</li> <li>Best practices for both using and deploying an o11y stack (visualization, alerting, metrics, logs, traces) - preferably with Grafana products (Grafana, Prometheus/Cortex/Enterprise Metrics, Loki/Enterprise Logs, Jaeger/Tempo).</li> <li>A proven track record of successful delivery of customer projects, preferably enterprise o11y implementations for large customers</li> <li>Excellent communication skills to communicate with customers, partners, and internal members.</li> <li>Kubernetes (kubectl, Helm, Tanka preferred).</li> <li>Experience with Cloud Platforms - AWS, GCP, Azure</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Points For:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Self-starter, adept at picking up new skills and technologies, and eager to break new ground.</li> <li>Vision to help us take our company to the next level.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Compensation & Rewards:</strong></p> </div> </div> <div> <p>In Germany<strong>,</strong> the base compensation range for this role is 109,700 EUR - 131,600 EUR. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.</p> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><div> <p><em data-stringify-type="italic">*Compensation ranges are country specific. title: Business Development & Sales Intern (w/m/d)
description: Über Valova Wir bauen die KI-Betriebsplattform für Europas Krankenhäuser, damit sich jede Ärztin und jeder Arzt auf die Patienten konzentrieren kann. Hinter jedem Fall steht eine Kette administrativer Aufgaben: Dokumentation, Kodierung, Abrechnung, Prüfungen, Planung. Sie läuft über getrennte Systeme und unzählige manuelle Übergaben . Wir starten dort, wo der Effekt ab Tag eins messbar ist: vom Fall bis zum Geldeingang . Valova kodiert jeden Fall, verteidigt ihn in der Prüfung und sorgt dafür, dass das Geld ankommt. Von dort übernehmen wir jeden Workflow eines Krankenhauses , bis ein agentisches System die Routine erledigt und Menschen über Ausnahmen entscheiden. Ein Team aus Ärzt:innen, Engineers, Strategieberater:innen und Start-up Profis. Vor Ort in München und Berlin . Wir freuen uns auf Dich! Warum diese Rolle zählt Als Praktikant:in im Business Development & Sales sorgst Du dafür, dass unser Vertriebsteam seine Zeit mit den richtigen Kliniken verbringt. Du findest und qualifizierst die Accounts, eröffnest die ersten Gespräche und buchst die Demos, die dann unsere Regional Sales Manager:innen wahrnehmen. Gleichzeitig baust Du den Motor dahinter mit auf: saubere Daten in unserem CRM Tool, Outreach-Sequenzen, die laufen, Dashboards, die zeigen, wo wir stehen, und KI-Automatisierungen, die unserem Team jede Woche Stunden sparen. Was Du bewirkst, siehst Du direkt anhand der gebuchten Termine, einer aufgebauten Pipeline und Prozessen, die weiterlaufen, lange nachdem Du sie aufgesetzt hast. Du sitzt nicht in der zweiten Reihe und schaust zu. Du baust den Vertriebsmotor mit auf, der Valova in Kliniken in ganz Deutschland bringt. Deine Rolle im Team Du berichtest an unseren VP Sales und arbeitest täglich mit unseren Regional Sales Manager:innen im Norden und Süden zusammen. Für viele Kliniken bist Du der erste Kontakt: Du recherchierst Accounts, gehst Inbound Leads nach, sprichst Entscheider:innen per Telefon, LinkedIn und E-Mail an und übergibst qualifizierte Termine an die Regional Sales Manager:innen, die sie bis zur Unterschrift bringen. Neben dem Outreach unterstützt du RevOps & Enablement, einen Bereich, den aktuell unser VP Sales selbst führt und gestaltest so von innen mit, wie unser Vertrieb arbeitet. Eng zusammen arbeitest Du außerdem mit unserem Marketing bei Kampagnen und Events sowie mit unseren Kodierexpert:innen und dem medizinischen Team, um zu verstehen, worauf es Kliniken wirklich ankommt. Deine Aufgaben Türen zu Kliniken öffnen: Du identifizierst vielversprechende Kliniken, von privaten Klinikgruppen über kommunale und ländliche Häuser bis zu Unikliniken, recherchierst die richtigen Entscheider:innen in Geschäftsführung, Finanzen, Medizincontrolling und Kodierung und gehst Inbound Leads schnell nach. Gespräche starten, die zählen: Du sprichst Kliniken per Telefon, LinkedIn und E-Mail an, mit Sequenzen, die auf den jeweiligen Kliniktyp und seine Herausforderungen zugeschnitten sind. Qualifizieren und Demos buchen: Du findest heraus, ob echter Bedarf besteht, wer entscheidet und wann und buchst Demos für unsere Regional Sales Manager:innen mit sauberer Übergabe. Unsere Pipeline up-to-date halten: Du hältst unser CRM sauber, baust Dashboards und bereitest Pipeline- und Forecast-Reportings für unseren VP Sales vor. Mit KI automatisieren: Du baust KI-gestützte Workflows und Automatisierungen für Recherche, Datenanreicherung und Outreach, damit unser Team weniger Zeit mit Routine und mehr Zeit mit Kliniken verbringt. Unseren Vertrieb mitgestalten: Du schreibst SOPs, schärfst Sequenzen und Playbook, unterstützt den Deal Desk bei Angeboten und Business Cases und recherchierst den Klinikmarkt und unseren Wettbewerb. Was Du mitbringst Studium: Du studierst BWL, VWL, Gesundheitsmanagement, Gesundheitsökonomie, Medizin oder ein anderes relevantes Feld und suchst ein Vollzeitpraktikum über mindestens sechs Monate. Erste Praxiserfahrung: Du hast bereits durch ein Praktikum oder eine Werkstudententätigkeit in Vertrieb, Business Development, Beratung oder einem Start-up praktische Erfahrung gesammelt. Keine Scheu vorm Telefon: Du gehst gern auf Menschen zu, auch auf erfahrene Entscheider:innen, und bleibst nach einem „Nein“ freundlich und hartnäckig. Strukturiert und datenaffin: Du bist sicher in Excel und hältst Daten gern sauber. CRM-Erfahrung, idealerweise mit Pipedrive, ist ein Plus. KI-nativ: Du nutzt KI-Tools täglich und hast Lust, Automatisierungen zu bauen. Erfahrung mit Tools wie n8n, Make oder Zapier ist ein Plus. Neugier aufs Gesundheitswesen: Du willst verstehen, wie Krankenhäuser funktionieren. Erste Kenntnisse in DRG-Systematik oder ICD/OPS-Kodierung sind ein Plus, kein Muss. Sprachen: Du sprichst Deutsch verhandlungssicher oder als Muttersprache und Englisch fließend. Arbeitsort: Du arbeitest vor Ort in unserem Büro in Berlin oder München Dir fehlen ein oder zwei Punkte, aber Du bist überzeugt, die richtige Person für diese Rolle zu sein? Dann bewirb Dich trotzdem. Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen. Was wir Dir bieten Ownership ab Tag eins: Du verantwortest Deine eigene Pipeline und treibst den Erfolg von Valova in Deine Vertriebsregion maßgeblich voran. Direkter Draht zur Vertriebsleitung. Du arbeitest täglich eng mit Stephan zusammen, unserem VP Sales und erfahrenen Scale-up-Executive. Keine Hierarchieebenen, kein wochenlanges Warten auf Freigaben. Lernen im Start-up-Tempo. Du erlebst hier in einem Jahr mehr als anderswo in drei. Ein Team, mitten in der Stadt. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam vor Ort im WeWork am Odeonsplatz in München und im WeWork in Berlin-Mitte. Dich erwarten voll ausgestattete Büros mit Kaffee, Meetingräumen und Phone Booths, eine zentrale Lage und gute Lunch-Spots direkt um die Ecke. Ein Team mit großen Zielen. Ärztinnen und Ärzte, Entwickler:innen und Kolleg:innen aus Vertrieb und Operations, die sich ehrgeizige Ziele setzen und alles daransetzen, sie gemeinsam zu übertreffen. Team-Events , die München und Berlin zusammenbringen, denn die Menschen, mit denen Du baust, sollten auch die sein, mit denen Du feierst. Woran wir Erfolg messen Nach 1 Monat kennst Du unser Produkt, unsere Zielkliniken und Pipedrive in- und auswendig, und Deine ersten Outreach-Sequenzen laufen. Nach 3 Monaten buchst Du regelmäßig qualifizierte Demos für unsere Regional Sales Manager:innen, unsere Pipedrive-Daten sind sauber und Deine ersten Dashboards und Automatisierungen sind live. Zum Ende deines Praktikums hast Du eine messbare Pipeline aufgebaut, die SOPs und Sequenzen, die Du geschrieben hast, sind Teil unseres Playbooks und Deine Automatisierungen sparen dem Team jede Woche Zeit. Die ganze Zeit über hat das, was Du in Gesprächen hörst, unsere Botschaften mitgeprägt und uns geholfen, den Markt besser zu verstehen. So läuft Dein Bewerbungsprozess Lade einfach deinen Lebenslauf samt Gehaltsvorstellung mit deiner Bewerbung hoch. Für die nächsten Schritte melden wir uns zeitnah bei dir: Kennenlernen (30 Min.): Wir lernen uns kennen, sprechen über deinen Werdegang und beantworten deine ersten Fragen. Gespräch mit unserem VP Sales (30 Min.): Wir sprechen über Deine bisherigen Erfahrungen und Deine Ideen für Valova und Deine Vorstellungen für das Praktikum. Case: Du führst mit uns ein kurzes Discovery-Gespräch oder einen Pitch anhand eines realistischen Klinikszenarios. Hier zeigst Du uns, wie du verkaufst. Referenzen: Wir sprechen mit zwei oder drei Personen, mit denen Du zusammengearbeitet hast, zum Beispiel ehemaligen Vorgesetzten, Kolleg:innen oder Kund:innen. Angebot: Wenn es für beide Seiten passt, hörst Du schnell von uns. Wir freuen uns auf Deine Bewerbung, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. title: Scientific Product Manager
description: About CuspAI CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering. We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock. We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters. We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us. The Role Due to rapid growth in our partner lab network, we are seeking a Scientific Product Manager to join our Product team and bring partner labs and their experimental workflows onto the CuspAI platform. Your impact This is an exciting opportunity to join the product team at CuspAI, working closely with materials scientists, ML researchers and platform engineers to make AI-driven experimentation work in real laboratories. As one of a small team of Scientific Product Managers, you will take ownership of a set of partner labs and the lab integration work around them, translating what each lab actually needs into requirements our engineers and ML researchers can build against. Alongside the product work, you will spend real time with your partners' teams and their experimental data. What You Will Do Product Requirements & Roadmap Shape and prioritise the roadmap for how experimental data, protocols and campaigns get into the CuspAI platform, together with your fellow Scientific Product Managers, the engineering lead and the wider product team. Write requirements, specifications and acceptance criteria that engineers can build from, covering experiment types, instrument integrations and LIMS/ELN connections, and work with the data team on the underlying data models and provenance. Contribute to decisions on what we build, what we integrate, and what we leave to partners' existing systems. Partner Lab Onboarding Lead technical discovery with the partner labs you take on: map their workflows, instruments, sample logic and data systems, and pin down the true experimental unit and the parameters that matter. Own onboarding for your partner labs from scoping to the first closed-loop campaign, and turn each onboarding into reusable patterns and documentation shared across the team so the next one is faster. Act as the main scientific counterpart for the partner labs you look after, and represent the product in partner meetings, workshops and conferences. Closed-Loop Campaigns Work with ML researchers to design optimisation campaigns (e.g. Bayesian optimisation) that respect real experimental constraints such as throughput, noise and failed samples. Define how platform-driven campaigns are validated, including benchmarks against manual or legacy workflows, success metrics and the evidence we bring to partners. Must Have Skills and Qualifications: PhD in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Chemical Engineering or a related experimental discipline, or equivalent experience in scientific research. Hands-on experience with high-throughput or automated experimentation (e.g. robotic synthesis, combinatorial libraries, automated characterisation, or self-driving / closed-loop labs) in industry, a national lab or research institute, or academia. Proven track record of translating scientific or process needs into requirements for engineers, software teams or automation vendors, and of validating that what was built works in the lab. Firsthand understanding of how experimental data is produced and where it fails: which metadata and provenance matter, instrument quirks, data quality issues, and what makes a dataset usable for machine learning. title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description: About Heidi Systems Heidi Systems builds the energy OS for real estate. We help property managers and owners get their heating, water and electricity meters online, see consumption in real time and run the yearly utility billing without paper, Excel and site visits. Submetering in Germany is still mostly analog. Meters get read by hand, data sits in PDFs, and tenants see their consumption once a year. We change that end to end: we install the meters and gateways in the building, collect the data and build the web platform property managers work in. We're a small team in Berlin. Product and engineering work directly with the founders, and what you ship lands with real customers fast. The role We're looking for a best-in-class frontend engineer. Someone whose code other engineers learn from. You'll be our senior frontend engineer and own the web platform end to end: architecture, code quality and the day-to-day experience of the property managers using it. The platform is a SvelteKit and TypeScript app. It shows consumption data per building and unit, flags anomalies, manages tenants and owners, and produces the documents for the yearly billing. A lot of it is data-heavy UI, and it has to be right, because the numbers end up on invoices. You'll work closely with our backend engineers and the founders, and you'll help onboard and mentor junior developers and interns as the team grows. What you'll do Own the frontend architecture of our SvelteKit app: routing, load functions, SSR, state and how we talk to the backend via oRPC Ship features end to end, from a rough idea with the founders to production, often before the design is final Build the data-heavy parts of the product: consumption dashboards, notification rules, tenant and owner management, billing documents Set up and maintain our component library on Tailwind and DaisyUI so the UI stays consistent as we add features Raise the bar on quality: strict TypeScript, Vitest coverage, code reviews, a sane PR flow Shape the API contract together with backend (types, Zod schemas, error handling) so frontend and backend stay in sync Mentor juniors and interns through reviews and pairing What you bring 5+ years of professional frontend experience, ideally at startups or other fast-moving product teams 2+ years building production apps with Svelte and SvelteKit, with a deep understanding of its reactivity model, stores, lifecycle, routing, load functions and SSR Strong TypeScript: strict mode, generics, utility types, and the judgment to know when types help and when they get in the way Hands-on with Tailwind CSS (DaisyUI is a plus) Experience with RPC-style APIs (oRPC, tRPC or similar) and typed contracts between frontend and backend Testing as a habit: Vitest, JSDom or comparable tooling Comfortable in a Unix environment (Linux or macOS), with Git, branches and PRs You've made architecture decisions on a real product and can explain the trade-offs You work well with little oversight and ship in small, frequent steps Fluent English, written and spoken You're in Berlin or willing to move, and you're in our office 2 to 3 days a week How we work Hybrid in Berlin. You're in the office 2 to 3 days a week. That's fixed. The rest of the week you work from wherever you like. Short paths. You talk to the founders directly, most decisions take one call. Real ownership. The frontend is yours to shape, and you'll set many of the standards the team builds on. Real impact. Your work runs in buildings across Germany and makes energy use visible where people live. Room to grow with the company as the engineering team gets bigger. Your next steps If you match most of these requirements and are ready to help digitize the building sector, we encourage you to apply. You will join a growing team where your work directly shapes the future of energy management in real estate. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Software engineer, AI model supply chain and package security
description: We build fast, modern developer tools in Rust, and a surprising amount of serious software runs on them. Pixi, rattler and rattler-build are open source and used by hundreds of thousands of developers: quant teams in finance, physicists at CERN, biotech labs, and humanoid robot companies you've probably seen videos of. We are also core maintainers of conda-forge, one of the largest open source package ecosystems, and we maintain RoboStack, which gets ROS running on any OS from a single lockfile. When that much software flows through your tools, security stops being optional. Every package that ends up on a laptop, a server or a robot should be traceable back to the source and build that produced it. We're building that for conda today, and we want to extend it to AI models. The engineering team is spread across Europe (Netherlands, Germany, UK, Moldova). This work is based in Berlin, and so is this role. The work Robots increasingly run learned models: vision transformers, RL policies, LLMs. Today those models are usually copied onto machines as large opaque files, with little record of where they came from or what changed. We think models should be shipped like packages: versioned, signed, verifiable, and updated efficiently. You'll work on two related areas. Package security. Signing and verification for conda packages with Sigstore, provenance from source to build to install, SBOMs, and mapping known vulnerabilities onto the packages people actually use. This work goes into Pixi, rattler and conda-forge, and is used by a lot of people. AI models as packages. Taking the same ideas to model artifacts. That includes: A provenance chain from training through packaging to deployment, with signatures that can be verified offline on air-gapped robots A model SBOM format, building on CycloneDX's ML-BOM Delta updates between model versions (full models, fine-tunes, LoRA adapters, quantized variants), so robots don't download gigabytes for a small change Compression that combines model techniques (quantization, pruning, distillation) with what package managers already do well (zstd, content-addressable storage), tuned to the target hardware and network Managing models that get fine-tuned on the robot itself: tracking where those variants came from, validating them, and syncing them back Testing the whole pipeline end to end on real models and real hardware, and measuring latency, bandwidth and model quality A lot of this is new. Part of the job is figuring out which approaches work, measuring them honestly, and writing up what you found. What we're looking for You don't need years of experience. You do need solid fundamentals, curiosity, and the patience to get security details right. Rust, or a strong background in C++, Go or Python and the wish to switch Interest in software supply chain security. Bonus if you've worked with Sigstore (Cosign, Rekor, Fulcio), TUF, in-toto, SLSA or SBOM formats Familiarity with ML in practice: you've trained or fine-tuned a model, know what a LoRA adapter or a quantized model is, and have used PyTorch or similar Basic understanding of cryptography as an engineer: signatures, hashes, certificates, and what they do and don't guarantee You like measuring things and are honest about results that don't work out You live in Berlin or are willing to move here It's a plus if you know package managers from the inside, have worked on model compression or edge inference, have robotics experience, or have contributed to open source. None of this is required. What we offer You'll work on problems few people have solved yet, together with the people who created Mamba, Pixi, rattler and RoboStack. Most of your work will be open source and used by a large community from day one. We pay a competitive Berlin salary, with 30 days of vacation, the hardware you want, a conference budget, and time for upstream open source work. We help with relocation within the EU. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Conseiller(ère) commercial(e) terrain expérimenté(e)
description: Indépendant | Rémunération à la commission uniquement | Territoire de vente local | Commissions déplafonnées À propos de l'opportunité Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l'aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants. En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d'opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route. Vous devrez justifier d'une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp. Vos missions Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes. Cibler les entreprises locales générant d'importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp. Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels. Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat. Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp. Établir des relations avec les chefs d'entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits. Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d'optimiser votre temps sur le terrain. Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes. Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux. Ce que nous recherchons Indispensable Au moins un an d'expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l'énergie, les technologies d'entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l'approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons. Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects. Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs. Des résultats démontrables en matière d'acquisition de nouveaux clients et d'atteinte d'objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu. La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections. Un bon sens de l'organisation et un suivi rigoureux. La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d'expérience et à persévérer. Une bonne compréhension du statut d'indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients. La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients. Atouts Un réseau existant de chefs d'entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp. Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente. Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain. Rémunération Il s'agit d'une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l'activité des commerçants apportés. Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner : Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions. Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème. Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème. Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans. Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois. Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales. Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d'activité du programme ; un barème Agent de 40 %, sans commissions résiduelles, peut s'appliquer. Les conditions d'éligibilité, les bases de calcul et les modalités de versement sont précisées dans le contrat et présentées avant tout engagement. Les commissions s'entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables. Formation et accompagnement Nous vous aiderons à vous familiariser avec les produits et leur commercialisation grâce à un parcours initial et à un accompagnement continu couvrant la prospection, les entretiens de vente, les démonstrations, la gestion des objections et l'accompagnement des clients. Les modalités du parcours initial et les prérequis à la commercialisation vous seront communiqués avant le démarrage. Votre interlocuteur SumUp vous apportera également son soutien en matière de développement territorial, d'analyse de vos opportunités et de conseils commerciaux, dans le respect de votre autonomie d'organisation.
