title: Head of ClinOps Data Management RWD/RWE
description: À propos de Lifen Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales peuvent transformer le système de santé, à condition qu’elles soient accessibles. Mieux les faire circuler, c’est réduire la charge administrative, mieux coordonner les soins et accélérer la recherche clinique. Depuis 2015, nous développons des solutions qui aident les professionnels de santé à partager les informations médicales et les chercheurs à exploiter des données de santé. Plus de 150 personnes travaillent chez Lifen, depuis nos bureaux et à distance. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé en France. Notre équipe L’équipe Clinical Ops intervient au cœur de nos projets de recherche clinique fondés sur des données de santé. Elle transforme des documents médicaux en données structurées, nécessaires à la constitution de cohortes patients et à la préparation des exports utilisés dans nos projets de recherche. Aujourd’hui, l’équipe structure environ 100 à 200 cas patients par semaine . Notre ambition : tripler cette capacité dans les 9 prochains mois, tout en maintenant un haut niveau de qualité des données. Pour y parvenir, nous cherchons une personne capable de reprendre le management de l’équipe, mais surtout de piloter le flux de production, d’anticiper la charge et de porter une démarche d’amélioration continue avec les équipes Produit, IA et Engineering. C’est un rôle à la croisée du management opérationnel, de la RWD et de l’amélioration de processus . Ce que tu feras chez nous Ta première mission sera de reprendre le pilotage de la production des cohortes afin d’en améliorer simultanément la qualité, la capacité de traitement et le niveau d’automatisation . Concrètement, tu seras amené·e à : Manager et faire grandir l’équipe Clinical Ops, en donnant un cadre clair aux priorités et en organisant l’activité quotidienne. Anticiper la charge et piloter la capacité de production afin de limiter les bottlenecks et de mieux absorber les variations de volume. Construire les outils de pilotage nécessaires pour avoir une vision fine du flux : volumes de patients, capacité de traitement, taux d’erreur, points de blocage et charge de l’équipe. Construire et orchestrer une roadmap d’amélioration continue permettant progressivement d’augmenter la capacité de traitement. Porter cette roadmap auprès des équipes Produit, IA et Engineering : rendre les besoins opérationnels visibles, suivre les livrables R&D et créer le rythme nécessaire pour que les améliorations soient effectivement délivrées. Garantir la qualité des cohortes et contribuer à la préparation des exports de données nécessaires aux projets de recherche. Ce que nous attendrons de toi Dans les premiers mois, nous attendrons de toi que tu développes une compréhension très fine du flux Clinical Ops : où se trouvent les blocages, comment évolue la charge et quels leviers permettent réellement d'améliorer la production. Ton succès se mesurera notamment à ta capacité à mettre en place un pilotage fiable de l’activité, à réduire les erreurs et les bottlenecks et à créer, avec les équipes Produit et R&D, un rythme d’amélioration continue suffisamment soutenu pour accompagner notre changement d’échelle. À horizon 9 mois, l’objectif est clair : passer d’environ 100–200 à 300–600 cas patients structurés par semaine, sans multiplier les ressources par trois. Ce que nous recherchons Must-have Nous chercherons en priorité trois éléments dans ton parcours : Une expérience réussie en startup ou scale-up , dans un environnement où les process, outils et responsabilités restaient à construire. Une expérience concrète de la Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence , idéalement autour de la constitution ou de l'exploitation de cohortes patients. Un background santé ou scientifique te permettant de comprendre les enjeux liés aux données médicales et à la recherche clinique. Nous attendons également : Une expérience confirmée de management d’équipe opérationnelle . Une expérience de structuration et de pilotage d’une activité complexe à partir de données et de KPI. Une capacité à passer d’un problème opérationnel très concret à un plan d’amélioration structuré. Une expérience de collaboration étroite avec des équipes Produit, Data/IA ou Engineering . Une capacité à faire avancer une roadmap transverse et à créer de l’accountability autour des livrables. Nice-to-have Un parcours en data management, biostatistiques, épidémiologie ou dans un domaine scientifique proche. Une expérience de structuration de registres, bases de données de santé ou cohortes RWD. Une familiarité avec les enjeux de recherche clinique et les interactions avec les autorités de santé. Une bonne compréhension des usages de l’IA et de l’ingénierie appliqués aux données de santé. Ta manière de travailler Tu as une vraie “just do it mentality” : face à un problème imparfaitement cadré, tu commences par comprendre les faits, tu structures le problème et tu mets rapidement en place les premières solutions. Tu es particulièrement à l’aise dans les environnements où il faut créer les outils plutôt que simplement les utiliser. Si le dashboard dont tu as besoin pour piloter ton équipe n’existe pas, tu es capable de le définir et de le mettre en place. Tu es structuré·e et organisé·e, mais pas bureaucratique. Tu sais entrer suffisamment dans le détail du flux pour comprendre les problèmes réels, tout en gardant une vision d’ensemble et en priorisant ce qui aura le plus d’impact. Enfin, tu sais faire avancer des équipes sur lesquelles tu n’as pas nécessairement d’autorité hiérarchique. Tu rends les problèmes visibles, explicites les priorités et crées le rythme nécessaire pour transformer les décisions en améliorations concrètes. Nos valeurs Embrace Complexity — Tu aimes comprendre un flux de données complexe, en identifier les points de rupture et transformer cette complexité en décisions concrètes. Bienveillance — Tu accompagnes une équipe au quotidien avec exigence, écoute et clarté. Real Impact — Tu améliores la qualité et la disponibilité des données qui permettent de faire avancer des projets de recherche clinique. Process de recrutement Échange de préqualification avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager, 30 minutes. Nous faisons connaissance, revenons sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les grandes lignes du poste. C’est aussi le moment de répondre à tes premières questions sur Lifen, l’équipe et le contexte. Entretien avec le VP Reasearch, 60 minutes. Nous revenons plus en détail sur ton parcours, ton expérience en RWD et en constitution de cohortes, ainsi que sur ton expérience de management et de pilotage d’activités opérationnelles. L’objectif est aussi de comprendre la manière dont tu structures et fais évoluer une organisation dans un environnement en croissance. Use Case avec des membres des équipes Clinical Ops et Produit, 60 minutes. À partir de situations concrètes, nous échangeons sur ta manière de structurer une cohorte RWD, d’analyser des problématiques opérationnelles et de construire des plans d’amélioration. Ce sera également l’occasion d’aborder la manière dont tu gères les enjeux humains et la collaboration avec des équipes transverses. title: Embedded Engineer
description: Accelerating embodied AGI. The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century. MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data. We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries. Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Embedded Engineer, you will own the firmware that runs on that hardware, from the first register write to the moment data leaves the device, so that what reaches our ML team is clean, synchronized, and trustworthy. What You Will Do Write and own the firmware for our data-capture hardware: sensors, motion-capture rigs, custom IoT setups, and prototype robots. Build real-time data acquisition: drivers, DMA, buffering, and streaming from many sensors at once without dropping a sample. Solve multi-sensor synchronization, calibration, and time-stamping so every data point lines up across devices and modalities. Bring up new boards with our Electrical Engineer and turn fresh hardware into working devices fast. Build the path from device to dataset: communication protocols, on-device logging, and handoff into our data pipeline. Work shoulder to shoulder with ML engineers. Your firmware decides what their training data looks like, and a timing bug can quietly ruin months of data. Make firmware reliable in the field: testing, OTA updates, error handling, and diagnostics that tell us what went wrong. Requirements Up to 5 years writing production firmware for embedded or IoT systems. Strong C/C++, experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar), and deep familiarity with microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar). Hands-on experience with peripheral interfaces and protocols: SPI, I2C, UART, USB, BLE, CAN, or similar. Experience integrating sensors in firmware: IMUs, cameras, depth sensors, force sensors, or similar. A strong understanding of how firmware decisions affect data quality, especially for EMG/EEG sensing: ADC configuration, sample rate, jitter, filtering, and buffering. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you write code accordingly. Comfortable debugging at the hardware boundary with a logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and debugger. Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice. High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. You are comfortable in 0-to-1 ambiguity, where the spec is "figure out what the spec should be". Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care. Fluent in English. German is a plus. Nice to Have A background in robotics, motion capture, or wearable devices. Experience with real-time or hard-deadline systems: audio, video sync, or robotic control loops. Experience with embedded Linux, time-sync protocols (PTP or similar), or low-power design. Familiarity with ML training pipelines. Even if you don't run them, you can read a training script. Open-source firmware contributions. Experience taking firmware from prototype to small-batch production: test fixtures, provisioning, and certification support. Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits: Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it. Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it. Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them. Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes. This is for you if: You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec. You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one. You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do. This is not for you if: You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. You would forward output you cannot explain. "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer. How We Hire We read every application and reply within five working days. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem. Then a decision, usually within a few days. Pay Transparency Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting. What We Offer Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter. Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval. A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage. Free food and drinks in the office. Equal Opportunity MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d’opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.</p> <p>Vous devrez justifier d’une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.</p> <h2>Vos missions</h2> <ul> <li>Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.</li> <li>Cibler les entreprises locales générant d’importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.</li> <li>Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.</li> <li>Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.</li> <li>Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.</li> <li>Établir des relations avec les chefs d’entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.</li> <li>Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d’optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.</li> <li>Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.</li> <li>Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.</li> </ul> <h2>Ce que nous recherchons</h2> <h3>Indispensable</h3> <ul> <li>Au moins un an d’expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l’énergie, les technologies d’entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l’approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.</li> <li>Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.</li> <li>Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.</li> <li>Des résultats démontrables en matière d’acquisition de nouveaux clients et d’atteinte d’objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu.</li> <li>La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections.</li> <li>Un bon sens de l’organisation et un suivi rigoureux.</li> <li>La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d’expérience et à persévérer.</li> <li>Une bonne compréhension du statut d’indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients.</li> <li>La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients.</li> </ul> <h3>Atouts</h3> <ul> <li>Un réseau existant de chefs d’entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.</li> <li>Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente.</li> </ul> <p>Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.</p> <h2>Rémunération</h2> <p>Il s’agit d’une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. title: Design Release Engineer -Airframe
description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. The Role We are looking for a Senior Design Release Manager to join our Airframe Team in Lausanne. In this role, you will bridge the gap between initial mechanical concept and full-scale manufacturing, taking complete ownership of the manufacturing dossier for our composite structures and airframe modules. From day one, you will drive Design for Manufacturability and Design for Assembly directly inside the design loop, before parts are frozen. You will set and hold the release standard, define geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, manage engineering change orders, and act as the single authority signing off on product transfer gates to manufacturing. What You Will Do Manufacturing Dossier Ownership: Own and maintain the complete transfer package for your designated airframe module, including controlled drawing packages, bill of materials structures, material and finish specifications, critical characteristics, and acceptance criteria. Design Loop Integration: Collaborate directly with mechanical design engineers early in the design phase to optimize composite layups, bonded joints, tooling interfaces, and tolerance stack-ups while design changes are still fast and low cost. Transfer Gate & Release Authority: Serve as the final authority on product release packages, evaluating transfer readiness against gate standards before handing hardware over to manufacturing operations. Disposition & Configuration Management: Manage engineering change orders and serve as the single technical contact for drawing dispositions, non-conformance reviews, and design clarification requests from the production line. Supplier & Manufacturing Alignment: Work closely with production operations and external suppliers to evaluate manufacturing constraints for composite structures and precision assemblies. Feedback & Continuous Improvement: Analyze initial production build data and floor feedback to refine manufacturing dossiers and update gate standards for future design iterations. What We Are Looking For Background: B.Sc . or M.Sc . in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline. Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerance Analysis: Practical mastery of applying GD&T with intent, performing tolerance stack-up analyses, and defining clear acceptance criteria. Composite Structures & Manufacturing: Strong working knowledge of composite materials, layup sequences, tooling limitations, cure cycles, and bonded structural joints. Drawing & Package Control: Proven experience owning released drawing packages, managing structured bill of materials, and running engineering change order workflows. Early Stage Execution: Demonstrated success integrating manufacturing and assembly principles directly into active design reviews rather than conducting post-design audits. Language Skills: Professional proficiency in both English and French to work fluidly across design engineering and French-speaking production teams. What We Offer Direct ownership in defining the release and manufacturing transfer standards for high-performance defense airframes. Active collaboration with design engineers early in the development cycle where engineering decisions carry high leverage. High-visibility technical impact across fast-scaling, hardware-centric production programs. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI. title: Characterization Lead
description: At Kandou , we are redeﬁning the economics of AI infrastructure. Our mission is to democratise AI by signiﬁcantly reducing the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) of hardware systems — a critical barrier to scalable adoption. Our proprietary MIMO-over-copper technology powers a high-performance, chiplet-based AI memory fabric that is both scalable and energy-efficient . Unlike traditional interconnects, our solution reduces power consumption signiﬁcantly while preserving high bandwidth and ultra-low latency — unlocking unprecedented efficiency for AI training and inference at scale. As Characterization Lead, you will own performance characterization of Zinal retimer silicon and the Randa Active Electrical Cable (AEC) channel. This is a Principal / Senior Staff individual contributor role with hands-on technical leadership. Your measurements will establish datasheet limits, channel classes and guard-bands for validation, manufacturing and customer specifications. Based primarily in Lausanne, you will work with silicon, signal integrity and validation teams, including channel characterization partners in Taiwan. Responsabilities · Lead silicon and channel characterization from measurement planning and bench setup through analysis, limit derivation and documented hand-off to validation. · Characterize TX/RX SerDes performance across process, voltage and temperature: swing, jitter, sensitivity, equalization, adaptation, CDR lock, BER bathtubs and shmoos. · Own channel measurements to at least 50 GHz, including de-embedding, insertion/return loss, mixed-mode S-parameters and common-mode and mode-conversion behavior. · Establish reference-paddle baselines and channel classes by gauge, reach and frequency; correlate HTDR-derived metrics with calibrated VNA measurements. · Derive datasheet limits and guard-bands from measured distributions, accounting for uncertainty, sample coverage and aging; maintain traceable datasets and limit revisions. · Assess carrier-loading and forwarded-clock tradeoffs using measured channel data and simulation, and translate the findings into supported configurations and characterization limits. · Characterize power, energy per bit and thermal behavior across operating modes and corners; investigate equalizer noise amplification and channel/thermal interactions. · Coordinate shared laboratory equipment and characterization milestones with validation teams; lead technical reviews and deliver limits in time for downstream qualification and screening. Essential Experience · 10 to 14 years of experience in SerDes/silicon characterization and/or high-speed channel and signal integrity characterization following degree completion. · Direct ownership of a characterization program whose results became datasheet limits or qualification thresholds for a shipping product. · Strong VNA measurement experience to 50 GHz or beyond, including de-embedding, mixed-mode S-parameters (Sdd/Scc/Scd/Sdc) and insertion/return-loss mask interpretation. · Hands-on TX/RX SerDes characterization, jitter decomposition, BER bathtubs, PVT shmoos and equalization/adaptation analysis. · Demonstrated common-mode and mode-conversion measurement depth, with the ability to distinguish channel behavior from fixture and calibration artifacts. · Statistical characterization and guard-band derivation across corners, with clear treatment of measurement uncertainty, sample size and aging. · Experience with VNAs, oscilloscopes of at least 50 GHz bandwidth, BERTs, jitter instrumentation, thermal forcing and ATE characterization load boards. · BS in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, with the technical communication and coordination skills to hand off defensible limits to validation and manufacturing teams. Essential Experience · Characterization leadership for shipping 100G/lane or 200G/lane retimers, PHYs, AECs or AOCs. · Deep mixed-mode characterization where common-mode behavior affects information transport and link margin. · Experience producing datasheet limits that a separate validation team independently qualified. · Multi-carrier or proprietary coding schemes, including OFDM-style subcarriers and space-time coding, and their characterization implications. · Published work or patents in channel modeling, de-embedding or SerDes characterization. · MS or PhD with a concentration in communications, RF/microwave engineering or signal integrity. description: About Orakl Oncology At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators. This is a hands-on scientific leadership role . You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme. You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions. What You'll Do Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve. Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality. Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses. Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims. Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes. Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations. Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks. Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications. Minimum Qualifications PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology. Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings. Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors , including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions. A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health , with clear intellectual and analytical contributions. Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures. Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations. Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English , including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers. Preferred Qualifications Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning. Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow. Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints. Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling. Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners. Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements. Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network. Who You Are A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time. title: Embedded System Lead Engineer
description: Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer. Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats. France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service. Pelagon is backed by Hexa , the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised. The role As Embedded System Lead Engineer , you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it. What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget. You will lead their technical development , from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come. These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge , on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role. The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it. What you'll own Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications. The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt. Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS). The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment. Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore. Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench. Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units. The hard problems you'll be solving These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point: Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling. Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell. Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible. Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it. Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean. Who we're looking for You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically: 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world. Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems . This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space. Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack : electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal. Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control. Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do. A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters. Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it. Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale. Why join now Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that. A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space. Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years. AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about. A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it. title: IA Engineer Intern (x/f/m) - Paris
description: <p>Join a team of passionate and committed people working to improve healthcare.</p> <p>At Doctolib, our tech teams build products and features that improve the daily lives of healthcare professionals and patients. We work in feature teams within an agile environment, in close collaboration with Product, Design, Data Science, and Business teams.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for an <strong>AI Engineer Intern</strong> to join our Tech team and contribute to the development of AI-powered features at Doctolib.</p> <p>You will work closely with experienced AI and software engineers to explore, prototype, evaluate, and improve AI-based solutions. This internship will give you the opportunity to gain practical experience across the different stages of an AI product, from experimentation to integration into a production environment.</p> <p>Your responsibilities will include:</p> <ul> <li>Contribute to the development of AI features and services under the guidance of experienced engineers</li> <li>Write Python code to support prototypes, experiments, evaluation tools, and backend components</li> <li>Experiment with large language models, prompting techniques, retrieval, and tool integration</li> <li>Contribute to automated tests and documentation for the components you develop</li> <li>Investigate issues, analyse results, and suggest improvements to your team</li> <li>Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and team rituals</li> </ul> <p>You will receive regular guidance from your mentor and teammates. The scope of your work will grow progressively as you become familiar with the codebase, the tools, and the technical challenges.</p> <h2><strong>Who you are</strong></h2> <p>Before you read on, if you do not have the exact profile described below but feel that this internship matches your skills and interests, we still encourage you to apply.</p> <p>You will be a great fit if you:</p> <ul> <li>Are in the final year of a degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a related field</li> <li>Have basic experience with Python through coursework, personal projects, research, or previous internships</li> <li>Have a basic understanding of programming concepts, data structures, and software development</li> <li>Are curious about artificial intelligence and interested in understanding how AI systems work</li> <li>Are comfortable communicating in English, both written and spoken</li> </ul> <p>It would be fantastic if you:</p> <ul> <li>Have worked on a project involving machine learning, natural language processing, or large language models</li> <li>Have used agentic frameworks like Langchain or Google ADK.</li> <li>Have experimented with AI APIs, prompting, retrieval, or conversational interfaces</li> <li>Have experience in taking products to production and supporting them with real users.</li> <li>Have some experience with Git, APIs, testing, or data analysis</li> <li>Have an interest in healthcare, privacy, or responsible AI</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Life at Doctolib Tech</strong></h2> <p>Our products are built on a cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile applications across several countries and healthcare systems.</p> <p>Even if Doctolib uses technologies like Ruby on Rails, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Swift, React Native, and many cloud-related technologies, the principal language you'll work on is Python.You will also have the opportunity to use AI-assisted development tools within our engineering practices.</p> <p>Discover our AI vision<a href="https://careers.doctolib.com/ai-careers/"> here</a> and learn more about our tech culture on the<a href="https://careers.doctolib.com/tech-doctolib/"> Doctolib Tech site</a>.</p> <h2><strong>What we offer</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A structured internship with dedicated mentoring</li> <li>The opportunity to work on real AI projects in a healthcare environment</li> <li>Technical learning sessions and access to internal engineering communities</li> <li>Access to AI tools for coding, development, and learning</li> <li>Meal vouchers</li> <li>Free breakfast in the office</li> <li>Up to 2 days of remote work per week</li> <li>A flexible workplace policy, depending on the team and location</li> <li>A collaborative and international working environment</li> </ul> <h2><strong>The interview process</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Coding Game</li> <li>Recruiter Interview</li> <li>Technical Interview</li> <li>Behavioral Interview</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Job details</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Internship, 6 months, full-time</li> <li>Location: Berlin, Paris, Nantes, Milan, or Amsterdam</li> <li>Hybrid work setup, up to 2 remote days per week</li> <li>Start date: March 2027</li> </ul> <h2><strong>We welcome everyone</strong></h2> <p>At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. We evaluate candidates based on their qualifications, motivation, and potential, without discrimination.</p> <p>The more diverse ideas are heard, the better our products can serve patients and healthcare professionals. We welcome applications regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, disability, or place of origin.</p> <p>To support an inclusive recruitment process, we invite you to leave personal information such as pictures and age off your application. If you require an accommodation during the interview process, please let us know.</p> <p>Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!</p> <h2><strong>Your data privacy</strong></h2> <p>All information provided through this application is processed by Doctolib for recruitment purposes. Là où la plupart des entreprises commencent à peine à mentionner l'IA dans leurs fiches de poste comptables, nous l'intégrons déjà au cœur de nos processus. Nous sommes en avance sur le marché — et nous assumons cette ambition.<br><br>Nous recherchons un(e) General Accountant Lead & Analyst pour rejoindre l'équipe General Ledger (GL). Ce rôle est bien plus qu'un poste de comptable senior : vous couvrirez l'intégralité des flux d'activités courantes (cycles fournisseurs, clients, immobilisations), avec un fort degré de reporting transverse en clôture, tout en portant un œil critique de contrôle de gestion sur les opérations. Vous serez à la fois garant(e) de la qualité des comptes, pilote de la transformation IA de l'équipe et business partner pour les directions Finance et opérationnelles.<br><br>Si vous cherchez un poste où la comptabilité rime avec impact stratégique, transformation digitale et leadership — ce rôle est fait pour vous.</p> <p class="p3"><strong>Vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li3">Piloter l'ensemble des cycles comptables courants (fournisseurs, clients, immobilisations, charges) et garantir leur fiabilité à l'échelle du groupe, en intégrant systématiquement une revue analytique de type contrôle de gestion (Réel vs Budget/N-1, détection d'anomalies, anticipation des impacts P&L)</li> <li class="li3">Orchestrer les prochain(e) membre de notre équipe si vous :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Disposez d'une formation supérieure en Comptabilité/Finance (DSCG, Master CCA, Grande École, DEC en cours ou class="li1">Avez une expérience significative en Big 4 (Manager/Senior Manager) et/ou en entreprise internationale en forte croissance</li> <li class="li1">Maîtrisez les normes IFRS (dont IFRS 16, 15) gestion dans votre pratique comptable</li> <li class="li1">Êtes à l'aise avec les ERP modernes et maîtrisez Excel/Google Sheets à un niveau avancé</li> <li class="li1">Parlez anglais couramment (C1/C2) — échanges quotidiens avec les équipes internationales</li> <li class="li1">Êtes un(e) leader naturel(le), capable de fédérer, mentorer et conduire le changement</li> </ul> <p class="p2"> </p> <p class="p1"><strong>Ce serait fantastique si vous aviez aussi :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Une expérience dans le secteur Tech/SaaS et/ou en environnement multi-pays</li> <li title: Engineering Team Lead, Serverless Containers
description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The team Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all. We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write. European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it. The Role This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it. You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU. On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own. That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure. What You Will Do Own the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero — across CPU and GPU. Make cold starts a solved problem: snapshotting, prewarming, image-layer caching, whatever it takes for scale-from-zero to feel instant. Treat AI workloads as the normal case: GPU-backed containers, streaming responses, long-lived connections, MCP servers that cost almost nothing while idle. Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions. Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone. Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback. Partner with Product Managers to turn platform decisions into a product developers want to deploy on. What We're Looking For 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write. You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped. You have built container or workload platforms — orchestration, scheduling, isolation, request routing — not just deployed onto someone else's serverless platform. Deep Linux: namespaces, cgroups, image layers, page cache — comfortable well below the application layer. Multi-tenancy instincts: density, isolation, and fairness when hundreds of customers share one fleet. Significant experience building complex backend or infrastructure systems. You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users. A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside. What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. title: Analytical Chemistry Specialist - Freelance AI Trainer Project
description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Analytical Chemistry Specialist – Freelance AI Trainer Project based in Switzerland. Are you an analytical chemistry expert interested in contributing to the next generation of artificial intelligence? This freelance opportunity allows you to apply your scientific expertise to train and evaluate advanced AI models designed to support scientific discovery, education, and laboratory research. You will assess AI-generated responses to complex analytical chemistry questions, identify inaccuracies, and strengthen scientific reasoning across a wide range of applications. Your work will help improve the accuracy, reliability, and practical relevance of AI-generated scientific knowledge. Working remotely and independently, you will contribute specialized insights to the development of more capable and trustworthy AI systems. This role is ideal for experienced chemistry professionals who enjoy solving complex problems, communicating scientific concepts, and exploring the intersection of chemistry and emerging technology. Accountabilities Evaluate AI-generated scientific content: Review responses to theoretical and practical analytical chemistry questions, assessing their factual accuracy, logical consistency, scientific rigor, and relevance to real-world laboratory applications. Apply specialized analytical chemistry knowledge: Develop and evaluate scenarios involving spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical analysis, quantitative chemical analysis, environmental testing, pharmaceutical analysis, and analytical method development. Assess advanced analytical techniques: Challenge AI models on mass spectrometry, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), gas chromatography (GC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) interpretation, trace analysis, titrimetric methods, and related instrumentation. Identify and document model weaknesses: Record reproducible errors, reasoning gaps, inaccurate interpretations, and other failure patterns to support systematic improvements in model performance. Contribute to AI training and evaluation: Provide detailed scientific feedback, propose corrections, and recommend improvements to prompts, evaluation criteria, and testing methodologies. Support scientific quality assurance: Apply principles of method validation, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and analytical data interpretation to evaluate the reliability of AI-generated outputs. Communicate scientific reasoning clearly: Explain conclusions, demonstrate analytical approaches, and document the steps behind technical judgments to help improve model transparency and reliability. Requirements Education: A PhD in analytical chemistry or a closely related chemical science discipline is preferred. Equivalent advanced expertise supported by relevant professional or research experience may also be valuable. Technical expertise: Strong knowledge of analytical chemistry principles, instrumentation, spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical methods, quantitative analysis, and analytical method development. Research or laboratory experience: Experience in laboratory-based research, analytical method validation, pharmaceutical or environmental testing, instrumentation-intensive studies, or related scientific applications is highly desirable. Specialized analytical skills: Familiarity with techniques such as mass spectrometry, HPLC, GC, NMR, trace analysis, titrimetry, and laboratory QA/QC procedures. Scientific evaluation skills: Ability to identify factual inaccuracies, assess scientific arguments, interpret experimental scenarios, and distinguish sound conclusions from flawed reasoning. Written communication: Excellent technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex scientific concepts clearly, precisely, and logically. Analytical thinking: Strong critical-thinking, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to break down complex problems and document reproducible findings. AI training readiness: Interest in evaluating AI-generated content, identifying model limitations, and contributing to the development of more reliable scientific AI systems. Working arrangements: Ability to work independently in a remote freelance environment, manage assignments effectively, and provide a secure computer and reliable high-speed internet connection. Benefits Competitive hourly compensation: A pay range of $8–$65 per hour , with the final rate determined by expertise, professional experience, and geographic location. The final offer may vary from the advertised range. Remote flexibility: Work remotely from India, with the flexibility associated with a freelance contract arrangement. Meaningful scientific impact: Help shape AI systems that may support scientific education, research, analytical problem-solving, and laboratory workflows. Intellectually stimulating work: Apply advanced analytical chemistry knowledge to challenging scientific questions and emerging AI evaluation tasks. Specialized professional contribution: Use your research, instrumentation, and laboratory expertise in an innovative technology-focused environment. Independent contractor arrangement: Manage your work in a freelance capacity, subject to project requirements and applicable engagement terms. Benefits clarification: This is a contract position. title: Banking Accounting Manager
description: <h2>🧡 About Alma</h2> <p>At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well-balanced trade. We originate several million consumer receivables a year, carry them for a few weeks, and refinance them off a deliberately light balance sheet through securitization vehicles (Fonds Communs de Titrisation) and our other funding lines. We are regulated as a société de financement and a payment institution.</p> <p>That changes what "accounting" means here. A lender's accounts are not a monthly deliverable produced at the end of a chain: <strong>they are the chain</strong>. Every payment event, every commission, every provision, every sale of receivables to an FCT has to become a journal entry that ties — to the transaction underneath it, to the general ledger above it, and to the prudential statements the regulator reads. At our scale and growth, this is a strategic topic, and one that is as much about data as it is about accounting.</p> <p>Today the chain exists: an internal core banking ledger we built ourselves, feeding NetSuite, feeding regulatory reporting. What it does not have is a single owner who understands it end-to-end, holds it to the standard a regulated lender needs, and evolves it as the business changes (geographies, products, licenses). That is the role we are opening.</p> <p>You will join an Accounting team inside a Finance organization of ~15 people covering Strategic Financing, FP&A, Accounting, Regulatory reporting and Controlling. You will report to the Head of Financing & Accounting, alongside the Financing team and the General Accounting Manager, who oversees corporate cycles, tax, statutory and consolidated accounts.</p> <p>This is a role with unusual ownership for its level: the banking accounting scope is yours from day one, and so is the data chain that produces it.</p> <h2>💼 About the job</h2> <p><strong>Own the accounting of the credit business:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own how the portfolio is represented in the books: origination, revenue recognition on merchant and customer commissions, deferred income, write-offs and recoveries, cost of risk and provisioning on performing and non-performing exposures.</li> <li>Own the accounting of our securitizations: sales of receivables to the FCTs, derecognition, discount and over-collateralisation, residual interests, servicing and management fees, hedging.</li> <li>Own the accounting of our funding: corporate debt, commercial paper, and the new funding instruments we add as the refinancing strategy evolves.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Own the core banking ledger:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Be the functional owner of the engine that turns business events into accounting: which event, which account, which currency, which date, which counterparty.</li> <li>Specify and validate the accounting schemes for every new product, partner and geography, and work with Engineering and Data on the ledger's model, its feed into the ERP, and the fixes when something drifts.</li> <li>Own the audit trail end-to-end — from a single €40 installment to a line in a prudential statement — and make it documented enough to be walked through by someone whose job is to challenge it.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Reinforce the control framework:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and automate the reconciliations that hold the whole thing together: ledger ↔ general ledger ↔ bank ↔ FCT reporting ↔ prudential statements.</li> <li>Shorten monthly close, incl. turning a manual, end-of-month, spreadsheet-based check into an automated, evidenced, repeatable control.</li> <li>Be Finance's counterpart to Internal Control and Periodic Control on everything accounting-data related.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Own regulatory reporting:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the production and the quality of our prudential and statistical reporting — solvency, large exposures, liquidity, and the statistical returns that go with them.</li> <li>Own the reconciliation tables that matter most: prudential statements to accounting balances, regulatory returns to the trial balance, own funds and RWA back to their audit trail.</li> <li>Own the reporting tooling and its data feeds, and work with the Regulatory and Financing teams on the evolutions of the prudential framework and on the treatment of our securitizations.</li> </ul> <h2>🧩 About you</h2> <p><strong>To succeed in this job:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have around 6-7 years of experience, ideally starting in audit of financial services — banks, consumer credit, asset management, securitization — in a Big 4 or a specialised practice, possibly with a first move in-house. You know how to build a number, prove it, and defend it line by line in front of people whose job is to challenge it.</li> <li>You know banking accounting for real: French banking GAAP, the PCEC, cost of risk, revenue recognition on credit products. Or you know financial services accounting well enough that the banking layer is a matter of months, not years.</li> <li>You actually enjoy controls at scale — reconciling large populations, hunting the anomaly, chasing the last twelve euros of a four-hundred-million balance until you know exactly where they went. If that sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this is not your role.</li> <li>You are autonomous and scrappy. On things to build, or on things that already exist.</li> <li>You are fluent in English and French — our documentation and our regulator are French, part of our business and our team are not.</li> </ul> <p><strong>And it will be nice if you also:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hold, or are working towards, the DEC (or CPA, ACCA, equivalent).</li> <li>Have been exposed to securitization — FCTs, SPVs, waterfalls, deconsolidation — or to a regulated credit institution from the inside.</li> <li><strong>You are autonomous on data.</strong> SQL is a daily tool, a data warehouse does not intimidate you, and your reflex in front of a five-million-row population is to query it, not to ask someone for a summary. This is the single most important line in this job description.</li> <li>Know NetSuite, BigQuery, dbt or Python.</li> <li>Have worked in a scaling fintech.</li> </ul> <p>Don't meet every single requirement? At Alma, we believe great hires come from diverse paths. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply. We value potential, curiosity and the ability to grow as much as experience.</p> <h2>🤑 Compensation & Benefits</h2> <ul> <li>Competitive salary based on 12 months</li> <li>Profit-sharing and employee savings plan</li> <li>Health insurance: 100% covered by Alma including family package</li> <li>Disability insurance: 100% covered by Alma</li> <li>Sport: partnerships with Gymlib and Classpass, or €30/month reimbursement for your sports activities</li> <li>Maternity/paternity leave: salary maintained at 100% during leave with no seniority requirement. Return to work at 4/5 schedule paid at 100% for 8 weeks.</li> <li>Sustainable Mobility Package (FMD): €544.80/year (excluding full-remote contracts)</li> <li>Meal vouchers: €10/day, 50% covered by Alma</li> <li>Mental health: free access to MindDay platform</li> <li>Paid time off: 25 days/year (+ additional paid leave granted for employees on executive contracts)</li> <li>Access to our Learning & Development Platform</li> <li>2 weeks of full remote possible per year in summer</li> </ul> <h2>🎯 Interview Process</h2> <ul> <li>Video call with a Talent Acquisition team member to understand your path, motivation & present you the role.</li> <li>Video call with Thibaut Mercier, Head of Financing, Regulatory Capital Optimization & Accounting</li> <li>Business case</li> <li>Video call with Stephanie Combe, CFO</li> </ul> <h2>🌍 Diversity & Inclusion</h2> <p>At Alma, we believe that diversity fuels innovation and makes our community stronger. We are committed to building a workplace where every person feels seen, respected, and empowered to do their best work whatever their gender, background, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, disability or lived experience. title: Lead Fraud & AML Ops
description: Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ? Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance. Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière. Notre vision Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes. Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise. Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients. À propos de Pennylane Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen. En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à : 💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant 💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1200 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches! 🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible 🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours 🚀 Déjà plus de 1 500,000 TPE/PME et plus de 7000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France ! Role context Pennylane currently operates around 50,000 business accounts through a BaaS model with Swan and is applying for Établissement de paiement and Société de financement licences. As we prepare to onboard new customers under our own licensed entity from mid-2027, we are building our first line of defence across onboarding, transaction monitoring, fraud and risk operations. As Transaction Monitoring & Fraud Operations Lead , you will be one of the first operational leaders in this greenfield setup. Reporting to the Head of FinCrime Operations, you will lead first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations across Pennylane’s payment activities within a single team. You will own first-line alert handling and fraud case management, with clear escalation paths to Compliance and Risk. Your mission will be to build and launch Pennylane’s first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations, then scale the team and its workflows as volumes grow—while maintaining strong decision quality, auditability and customer protection. This is a high-autonomy role with direct exposure to a strategic regulatory project and close collaboration with Product, Compliance and Risk. You will help shape how Pennylane protects the financial activity of French SMEs as it brings more of its regulated operations in-house. Responsibilities Own end-to-end first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for business customers, ensuring that alert triage, investigations, customer outreach and escalations are completed in line with policies set by Compliance and Risk and within agreed SLAs. Translate AML/CFT and fraud policies into operational procedures, decision trees and analyst playbooks, and provide evidence-based recommendations on alert quality and operational bottlenecks. Review complex or high-risk alerts within the first-line mandate, oversee post-onboarding fraud cases and ensure that escalations, customer complaints and law-enforcement requests are handled with complete, auditable records. Implement the QA and reporting framework, monitor operational and risk indicators, and support Compliance during controls testing, audits and regulatory reviews. Recruit, onboard and lead the transaction monitoring and fraud analyst team, combining hands-on support with effective coaching and a culture of rigour, accountability and continuous learning. Establish the team’s performance and capacity framework, covering SLAs, productivity, quality, backlogs, false-positive rates and hiring needs. Partner with Product and Tech to test and improve transaction-monitoring, fraud and back-office workflows, prioritising automation while identifying the controls and decisions that should remain manual. First 6–12 months Deliver approved operating procedures, analyst playbooks and escalation rules before go-live. Establish a capacity and hiring plan based on observed alert volumes and handling times. Validate that alert queues, evidence collection, account measures and second-line handovers work operationally before launch. By go-live, have first-line monitoring operational for new customers, with trained coverage, agreed SLAs, documented QA controls and named escalation owners. What we’re looking for Significant experience in transaction monitoring, fraud or broader financial-crime operations within a regulated financial-services environment, including ownership of operational performance and complex case decisions. Proven experience leading and developing an operational team responsible for alert queues or investigations, combining effective coaching with a hands-on player-coach approach when needed. Strong understanding of first-line alert handling: triage, investigation, typology, escalation, and the difference between a fraud case and an AML case. Good working knowledge of French and European AML/CFT expectations, including ACPR and TRACFIN requirements, and experience translating policy into SOPs, decision trees and analyst guidance. Experience working with Product or Tech on workflow or tooling changes. Sound judgement on what to automate, what to sample and what to escalate. Ability to use operational metrics to manage quality, backlogs and capacity. Ability to make structured, well-documented decisions under pressure and communicate complex cases clearly to operational and compliance stakeholders. Comfort building operations in a greenfield environment where volumes are still uncertain and tooling is evolving. Exposure to ACPR expectations, a licensing programme, a BaaS migration or law-enforcement requests would be an advantage. Languages, presence and location Fluent French and English are mandatory. Based in France, with a strong preference for Paris. Regular on-site presence in Paris is expected. Partial remote is possible. This is not a fully remote role. Why join Build first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for a new regulated entity from the ground up. Shape the operating model before launch, rather than inheriting fixed processes and tooling. Take ownership of a critical domain with a direct impact on go-live readiness, customer protection and responsible growth. Work closely with Operations, Compliance, Risk, Product and Tech on a strategic company project. Recruitment Process 1. Interview with Lucie (30-45 min), Senior Recruiter 2. Interview with Maxime (1h), General Manager 3. Case Study with Laurent and Léa (1h) 4. Last round with Stanislas and Felix (45 min) 🎁 Ce que l’on peut t'offrir : 🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind) 🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile) 🏝 Entre 6 et 12 jours de RTT supplémentaires aux 5 semaines de congés payés 🧑‍💻 Un budget dédié chaque mois pour tous nos Pennylaners, favorisant le travail depuis la maison ou en espace de coworking 🏢 Une facilité d’accès à nos bureaux, situés à quelques minutes de Saint Lazare en plein cœur de Paris 💵 Une enveloppe de BSPCE 🏃‍♀️ Un accès à 8000 salles de sport partout en France et plus de 300 activités de bien-être via notre partenaire Gymlib 💻 Un Mac 🎉 Nous pratiquons de nombreux sports ensemble et avons à cœur de nous réunir régulièrement autour d’événements d’entreprise tels que les Tech Days (qui permettent aux Pennylaners en remote de se réunir tous les 3 mois) ou notre séminaire d’entreprise qui a lieu une fois par an, et qui favorise de grands moments de cohésion pour toutes et tous. Pour t'épanouir chez Pennylane, il faudra: -Parler anglais (le niveau est évalué et apprécié en fonction du département auquel tu postules) -Apprécier travailler dans un environnement en changement constant -Faire de la collaboration une priorité au sein de son équipe ou avec d'autres parties prenantes -Avoir un recul suffisant pour prioriser les actions à fort impact business dans son activité quotidienne. title: Backend & Applied AI Engineer

Our company offers remote monitoring solutions in oncology, gastroenterology and psychiatry, based on the collection of ePROs combined with AI technologies.
