title: Technical Implementation Manager / Chef.fe de Projet Déploiement Technique
description: Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides. Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, deux choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission. Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé. 🧩 Notre équipe Customer Operations Chez Lifen, nous déployons nos solutions dans les hôpitaux de toute la France pour améliorer le quotidien des soignants et la qualité des soins. L'équipe Customer Operations est le pont entre nos produits et les établissements de santé. Elle accompagne chaque hôpital dans l'implémentation de nos solutions : Lifen Documents & Lifen Intégration. Notre équipe est composée de Project Managers et d'Operations Managers, tous pilotés par Loïc, notre Lead Customer Operations. Nous recherchons aujourd'hui un profil à la croisée de la technique et de la gestion de projet : une personne capable de piloter un déploiement client de bout en bout, mais aussi de prendre en main les aspects techniques de l'intégration de nos solutions. Si tu aimes autant comprendre comment fonctionnent les systèmes informatiques que coordonner les parties prenantes d'un projet, ce poste devrait te plaire ! 🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous En tant que Technical Implementation Manager, tu seras responsable de la mise en œuvre technique de nos solutions dans les établissements de santé, depuis le cadrage initial jusqu'à leur mise en production. Ton rôle ? Faire en sorte que nos solutions s'intègrent correctement dans les systèmes d'information hospitaliers, tout en garantissant le bon déroulement des déploiements. Concrètement, tu seras amené(e) à : 🔧 Piloter et réaliser les déploiements techniques Configurer et déployer nos applications dans les environnements informatiques de nos clients. Mettre en place et configurer les flux d'interopérabilité entre nos solutions et les systèmes d'information hospitaliers (notamment HL7). Travailler avec les équipes IT des établissements sur les prérequis techniques : serveurs Windows, réseau, connectivité, VPN, SFTP, certificats et sécurité. Diagnostiquer et résoudre les problèmes techniques rencontrés lors des installations et des mises en production. 📋 Gérer tes projets d'implémentation de bout en bout Organiser et animer les réunions de cadrage technique avec les établissements de santé. Identifier les besoins, les contraintes et les prérequis techniques nécessaires au déploiement. Coordonner les différents interlocuteurs (DSI, équipes techniques hospitalières, chefs de projet, équipes internes Lifen) pour assurer la bonne avancée des projets. Suivre les différentes étapes du déploiement, anticiper les risques, lever les blocages et garantir la qualité des mises en production. 🔍 Garantir le bon fonctionnement de nos solutions Réaliser les tests techniques et fonctionnels avec les clients afin de valider le bon fonctionnement de nos solutions de bout en bout. Analyser les incidents et identifier leur origine (configuration, connectivité, flux, application...). Assurer le support technique de niveau 2 en collaboration avec les équipes Support, Produit et R&D. Surveiller les flux et les certificats pour anticiper les dysfonctionnements. 🤝 Être un interlocuteur technique de confiance pour nos clients Échanger directement avec les équipes IT des hôpitaux pour résoudre les problématiques d'intégration. Savoir expliquer des sujets techniques à des interlocuteurs moins techniques. Comprendre les contraintes du terrain pour proposer des solutions adaptées, fiables et pérennes. 🚀 Contribuer à l'amélioration continue de nos déploiements Documenter les configurations, les procédures et les problématiques rencontrées. Identifier des opportunités pour standardiser, automatiser et fiabiliser nos déploiements. Faire remonter les retours terrain aux équipes Produit et R&D pour contribuer à l'évolution de nos solutions. Développer progressivement une expertise sur l'ensemble de nos produits. ⭐️ Ce que nous recherchons Nous recherchons avant tout un profil technique qui aime gérer des projets, résoudre des problèmes concrets et travailler directement avec les clients. 🖥️ De solides bases techniques Tu as une expérience pratique dans le déploiement, l'intégration ou l'administration de solutions logicielles et tu es à l'aise avec plusieurs des environnements et technologies suivants : Systèmes : environnements Windows Server, administration système, GPO, installation et configuration d'applications. Réseaux et connectivité : TCP/IP, VPN, SFTP, certificats et notions de sécurité informatique. Intégration applicative : compréhension des échanges de données entre applications, des flux et des problématiques d'interopérabilité. Diagnostic technique : capacité à analyser des logs, identifier l'origine d'un incident et conduire sa résolution. Tu n'as pas besoin d'être expert(e) sur chacune de ces technologies, mais tu dois avoir suffisamment de bagage technique pour être autonome face aux problématiques d'un déploiement. 📋 Une expérience en gestion de projet technique Tu as déjà coordonné des déploiements ou des projets d'intégration de logiciels chez des clients, en collaboration avec plusieurs interlocuteurs techniques et métiers. Tu sais organiser un projet, suivre ses étapes, anticiper les risques et faire avancer les sujets jusqu'à leur résolution. 🤝 Une vraie aisance dans la relation client Tu es capable d'échanger aussi bien avec un administrateur système ou un responsable IT qu'avec un chef de projet ou un utilisateur métier. Tu sais vulgariser les sujets techniques, poser les bonnes questions et construire une relation de confiance avec tes interlocuteurs. 🛠️ Un état d'esprit orienté résolution de problèmes Tu aimes comprendre comment les choses fonctionnent, investiguer lorsqu'un problème survient et trouver des solutions concrètes. Tu es autonome, rigoureux(se), proactif(ve) et tu n'hésites pas à mettre les mains dans le cambouis plutôt que de simplement coordonner les actions des autres. 🏥 Une connaissance du secteur de la santé est un plus Une expérience dans un établissement de santé, chez un éditeur de logiciels de santé ou dans l'intégration de systèmes d'information hospitaliers sera particulièrement appréciée. Une connaissance des standards d'interopérabilité en santé, notamment HL7, est également un vrai atout. Mais ce n'est pas indispensable : si tu disposes d'un solide socle technique et d'une expérience en déploiement logiciel, nous pourrons t'accompagner dans la découverte des spécificités du secteur hospitalier. 💎 Nos avantages Package entre 40-47K€ Mode de travail : Commuter (3 jours/semaine au bureau) Une carte Swile avec 9 €/jour (50 % Lifen) Une mutuelle santé incluant médecine alternative et soutien en santé mentale (55 % Lifen) 30 €/mois pour concerts, musées ou même pour rembourser ton abonnement Spotify Une prise en charge à 100 % du congé maternité et paternité + 5 jours enfants malades par an 1 offsite avec ton équipe par semestre + 1 offsite global Lifen par an + 1 monthly où nous nous retrouvons tous au bureau à Paris Et enfin : une politique de rémunération transparente et graduelle 👥 Notre process de recrutement Premier échange RH avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager (30 minutes) Entretien manager avec Loïc (45 minutes) Cas pratique technique à préparer chez soi, puis restitution et discussion avec l'équipe dans nos locaux (1 heure) Entretien final avec deux Lifeners d'une autre équipe Soigner mieux en soignant ensemble, c'est aussi agir avec bienveillance. À l'image du secteur dans lequel nous évoluons, nous favorisons la diversité, l'inclusion et l'équité. Nous mettons en valeur vos compétences et votre savoir-faire, et bannissons toute forme de discrimination, qu'elle soit sexuelle, religieuse ou politique. title: First RevOps
description: At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding. Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work. Legacy software hasn’t helped, it’s made things slower, more complex, and more frustrating for care teams. We believe AI agents can change that. Our technology combines Large Language Models with system-level automation to handle real work inside existing hospital tools. No integrations, no disruption. Our first agent automates coding workflows and frees up time for medical staff to focus on patients. We launched in 2024, are backed by top investors (Index, Frst, Y Combinator, Hexa, Kima Ventures, Better Angle), and we’re just getting started. The future of healthcare isn’t just digital — it’s automated. Come help us build it ! Context Our coding agent is live in 70 hospitals across France. In March, we raised $20M from Index Ventures to push it further and build what comes next: billing, admissions, patient records. The next six months are going to move fast. We'll double to +60 people, open Germany, and triple the size of our Revenue team. Today, too much of how we run the company still depends on manual work and tools that don't talk to each other. Nobody owns this problem yet, it will be yours. Your mission Make sure Parallel can double without drowning in manual work. Attio, our CRM, will be your main tool, and you'll run it end to end. You'll also sit with each team, see what they still do by hand, and automate it yourself. On top of that, you'll work on Sales, Marketing and Finance Ops topics, like billing, cash tracking and commissions. title: Solution Consultant - R&D
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW Benchling Solution Consultants (SC) are the primary solution leads with Benchling’s largest customers and prospects. Their solutions are deployed into complex enterprise IT environments, interfacing with other vendor solutions, lab instruments, and legacy applications. This is a highly visible role that partners with both external and internal teams to develop the optimal solutions that drive the most value for our customers. The SC is a pre-sales role, and as such works closely with Benchling sales leadership, account executives, professional services, and product leaders to ensure the best solutions are presented. SCs work with senior scientific and IT leaders from prospects and customers, to establish credibility and confidence from the first meeting, and to create solutions based on cutting-edge technologies. The SC must be comfortable with Life Sciences R&D processes and scientific concepts, have experience with enterprise SaaS solutions, and be adept at working with internal and external leaders and stakeholders. You must work as a trusted adviser to translate customer objectives into detailed solutions and effectively communicate and demonstrate those solutions to prospects and customers. RESPONSIBILITIES Effectively partner with account executives, SC peers, and leadership to create account and deal strategies that lead to selection, planning out customer engagements that lead to compelling solutions. Manage organized discoveries to uncover customer needs and requirements that relate to decision criteria and key business issues. Craft solutions based on Benchling capabilities, industry best practices and standard R&D functions, with data models and processes that map to the customer or prospects' science and that fit into their current technology landscape. Present and demonstrate the solution in a persuasive way based on key messages, decision criteria, and key business issues. Manage customer questions and objections and resolve concerns. Ensure that the solution is presented competitively, with awareness of alternatives including build in house. Engage with product management to provide insight into prospect and customer needs and industry trends. Influence the roadmap for market success. Ensure that the roadmap is clear to customers as required to influence buying decisions. Provide leadership by creating reusable solutions, content, and trainings for key areas. Work with the extended team to ensure that they are successful and learn from your expertise. Mentor and partner with other SCs to build their success. QUALIFICATIONS Master’s in Biology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Biochemistry, Chemistry or similar Life Science field, with a minimum of 4 years of work experience, ideally customer facing. Experience with scientific/informatics software such as LIMS, ELN, or others preferred. Familiarity with antibody engineering software is a plus. Experience in demonstrating scientific software in a pre-sales setting to top 20 biotech and pharma companies is highly desired. Demonstrated capacity to effectively model scientific data, and craft solutions, based on product knowledge and industry best practices. Prior experience in demonstrating and supporting research instruments, reagents or software desired. Understand research technology generally adopted by biopharma companies. Have an agile and adaptable mentality, and can quickly implement new customer engagement processes. Ability to establish as a trusted advisor for scientists, and successfully pitch to scientific buyers. Must be fluent in English. Fluency in German or French is a plus. Willingness to travel to customer sites 25-30%. Master’s in Biology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Biochemistry, Chemistry or similar Life Science field, with a minimum of 4 years of work experience, ideally customer facing. title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description: Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale. We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does. Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place. Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published. Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you. 1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against. 2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on. 3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not. 4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough. Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster. A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job. If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold. 1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus. 2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer. 3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome. You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter. 4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus. Why us? Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate. No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title. We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one. Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP). Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible. Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together. Process Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are. Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going. Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves. Meet the team in our Zurich office. A mutual decision, before we welcome you to the team. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible. </span> <br><span data-contrast="auto"> </span> <br><span data-contrast="auto">Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":true,"134233118":true,"201341983":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p></div><p> </p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">About BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. </span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing, and delivering transformative medicines for patients living with genetic diseases and genetically defined cancers. Since our founding in 2015, we have built a diverse portfolio of more than 20 drug development programs, ranging from early discovery to late-stage clinical trials, across multiple therapeutic areas including precision oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, and renal disease. We have already achieved regulatory approval for three therapies and continue to advance promising science from academia into meaningful treatments for patients worldwide. </p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Who We Are </span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a global biotechnology company with our Global Headquarters located in San Francisco, USA, and our International HQ located in Zug, Switzerland. Since establishing our European presence in 2021, we’ve been building empowered, high-performing teams across countries — with experienced colleagues who move quickly, take ownership, and are fueling the company’s international growth. </p> <p>At BridgeBio, you’ll find an energetic and collaborative culture where pragmatism meets bold decision-making. We embrace uncertainty with confidence, guided by our commitment to making a meaningful impact for patients. Our people are trusted and empowered, united by urgency, purpose, and the drive to advance science for patients around the world. </p> <p>To learn more about our story and company culture, visit us at <a href="https://bridgebio.com">https://bridgebio.com</a></p> <p><strong><u>What You’ll Do</u></strong></p> <p>You will report to the VP, Head of Market Access, International and work closely with international Market Access, regional brand team, and heads or markets access in BridgeBio clusters as well as with field-based colleagues across multiple geographies, to drive strategic initiatives that support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients globally.</p> <p>Your primary purpose will be to secure timely, sustainable patient access to the company’s products by shaping the value narrative, and leading pricing and reimbursement strategies and execution across multiple international markets. This includes oversight of related dossiers, negotiations, and cost coverage approaches. In this role you ensure alignment of Market Access ambitions with clinical value and global pricing interdependencies.</p> <p>You will also be a core member of the International Market Access team, contributing to global decision-making and ensuring alignment across regions while representing diverse market perspectives.</p> <p>This role requires strong collaboration with cross-functional colleagues and external stakeholders across multiple countries to ensure high-quality execution and impact. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in Market Access processes across several international markets and experience introducing innovative therapies in a global biotech environment. You are eager to make a meaningful contribution in pre-launch and launch phases, particularly within rare diseases and orphan conditions, and bring strong communication skills, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong><u>Responsibilities</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Represent the payer perspective within cross-functional, cross-regional commercialization teams thereby optimizing pricing and market access of the asset.</li> <li>Closely collaborate with HEOR and clusters' leadership teams, Marketing and Clinical Development counterparts to ensure value and access optimization for the asset.</li> <li>Lead early payer engagement with key HTA/payer bodies (e.g. NICE UK, G-BA Germany) to inform evidence generation strategy, value proposition and reimbursement dossiers development.</li> <li>Interact with internal and external experts in pricing, health economics, patient advocacy, health technology assessment authorities, government policy makers and payers as required to execute Pricing & Reimbursement objectives.</li> <li>Provide hands-on support and train local access teams on negotiation strategy and ensure HTA and reimbursement submissions are aligned to the Global and International strategy.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong><u>Where You’ll Work  </u></strong></p> <p>This is an office role based and requires in-office collaboration 2-3x per week in our Zug Office.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong><u> </u></strong><strong><u>Who You Are</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Extensive experience leading HTA submissions and pricing negotiations across multiple international markets, ideally including Europe and other global regions, particularly in rare diseases and orphan conditions.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of international healthcare systems, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and regulatory environments.</li> <li>Experience generating and leveraging data for HTA submissions and pricing negotiations, with a strong external network of agencies and stakeholders.</li> <li>Comfortable presenting at senior levels and engaging with external thought leaders globally.</li> <li>Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional and multicultural teams (including external partners).</li> <li>Knowledge of product commercialization processes with a hands-on, solution-oriented mindset for building scalable processes and documentation.</li> </ul> <p><strong><u>Rewarding Those Who Make the Mission Possible</u></strong></p> <p>We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return.</p> <ul> <li>Market leading compensation</li> <li>Hybrid work model - we value your flexibility in how you work, but encourage time in the office to strengthen our culture, collaboration, and sense of community</li> <li>We provide career development through regular feedback, continuous education and professional development programs</li> <li>We celebrate strong performance with financial rewards, peer-to-peer recognition, and growth opportunities.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p> </p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>As a global company, our comprehensive benefits may vary based on location.  <span data-contrast="auto">We have high expectations for our team members. description: <h3>Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default</h3> <p>Proton was founded in 2014 by scientists from CERN on a simple truth: <strong>privacy is a fundamental human right</strong>. Since then, we've built the world's largest encrypted email service (Proton Mail) and expanded into Proton VPN, Proton Drive, Proton Pass, and Proton Calendar — tools used by millions globally to protect their freedom, fight censorship, and keep their data safe. In some situations, Proton has literally helped save lives.</p> <p>We are profitable, independent (no VC control), and selectively hire from the top ~1% of applicants. Our 700+ team members across 50+ countries come from leading organizations and elite academic backgrounds. We move fast, keep hierarchy light, and prioritize impact over optics. If you want to do meaningful work with exceptionally high-caliber people, this is it. Check our open-source projects <a href="https://proton.me/community/open-source">here</a>.</p> <p class="Lexical__paragraph"><strong><strong class="Lexical__textBold" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Purpose of the role:</strong></strong><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">  </span></p> <p class="Lexical__paragraph"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Storage is at the very center of everything we do. In this role you will join the Storage SRE team that is responsible to automate, scale, enhance and run our Storage infrastructure. The office locations we hire into for this role are Geneva/Switzerland or Paris/France.</span></p> <p class="Lexical__paragraph"><strong><strong class="Lexical__textBold" style="white-space: title: Technical Project Manager (Efector Development)
description: As Destinus scales its vehicle programmes, we are looking for a dedicated Technical Project Manager to own execution across the full vehicle development stack – from propulsion and structures through avionics integration, ground support equipment, and qualification. This frees our engineers to focus on technical depth and our team leads on strategic leadership. As one of the first hires in this group, you will manage a programme and help build the PM structure itself alongside team leads and fellow TPMs. You own execution – schedule, cross-disciplinary coordination, risk, and delivery. The engineers run the technical depth; you run the programme. What You’ll Do · Own end-to-end execution of vehicle-level and subsystem product development programmes – from kick-off through hardware build, test campaigns, qualification, and delivery · Build and maintain programme plans spanning propulsion, structures, avionics, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and regulatory dependencies; identify and resolve critical path risks early · Run programme reviews and cross-functional coordination meetings; keep decisions documented and actions closed · Work closely with engineering leads across disciplines to track technical progress and translate it into clear programme status · Coordinate system integration activities – ensuring interfaces between subsystems (propulsion, structures, avionics, GSE) are managed, dependencies tracked, and integration milestones owned · Manage external dependencies: supplier lead times, test facility scheduling, regulatory submissions, and customer milestones · Proactively flag scope creep, resource conflicts, and schedule risk to leadership – with options, not just problems · Contribute to building the PM structure, tools, and ways of working for the department alongside team leads and fellow TPMs Requirements Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, systems, or a related engineering discipline · 5–8 years in a hardware-heavy development environment; at least 2 in a project management, programme coordination, or technical lead role – career PMs without hardware exposure will not be considered · Background in aerospace, defence, or a similarly regulated hardware domain; familiarity with vehicle-level or system-level development and qualification cycles is essential · Experience managing cross-disciplinary programmes spanning multiple engineering domains (structures, propulsion, avionics, or similar) is a strong advantage · Able to manage multiple concurrent projects across engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and testing · Strong systems thinking – able to see the full picture, spot where the hard problems are likely to sit, and know when to dive into detail without losing the overall programme · Strong planning skills – able to build a programme schedule from scratch, identify critical path, and keep it current · Comfortable building structure in an ambiguous environment; pragmatic over bureaucratic · Clear, direct communicator in English; German is an advantage Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: System Integration Engineer (System Engineer - Effector Development)
description: The Destinus engineering team is seeking a Systems Engineer to lead the system-level definition and technical development of our effector programmes. This role sits at the centre of the development effort – bridging operational requirements and technical execution across propulsion, structures, avionics, and seeker. The ideal candidate brings a defence systems background and understands the full development lifecycle of a guided effector – from ConOps and requirements through subsystem design, integration, and qualification. They are technically credible across multiple domains, rigorous in their systems thinking, and effective at driving alignment across disciplinary teams. What You’ll Do · Define and own system-level requirements for effector programmes – capturing operational needs, translating them into technical requirements, and maintaining traceability from ConOps through to subsystem specifications · Develop and maintain ConOps and operational scenario definitions; work with the customer and programme stakeholders to ensure operational intent is correctly reflected in the system design · Define and manage technical interfaces between subsystems (propulsion, warhead/pyrotechnics, structures, avionics, guidance, and GSE); own the ICD and IRS documentation · Lead trade studies and make-or-buy analyses to identify the best technical and commercial solutions at system and subsystem level · Identify and track critical components and subsystems; define mitigation strategies for technical risk and drive resolution through the engineering team · Lead or support system design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR) and prepare the associated technical baseline documentation · Coordinate system integration activities across propulsion, structures, avionics, and external teams; ensure interfaces are closed and integration milestones are met · Support verification and validation planning; define the V&V approach at system level and ensure it flows down to subsystem test plans Requirements What You’ll Need · Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace, Systems, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field · 5–8 years of systems engineering experience on defence or weapons system programmes – rockets, missiles, or guided weapons are a strong advantage; a background in aerospace or space launcher development is also suitable · Proven experience defining and managing system requirements and interfaces across multi-disciplinary teams in a defence acquisition or development environment · Hands-on experience with ConOps development, trade studies, and make-or-buy decision frameworks · Familiarity with system design review processes (SRR, PDR, CDR) and the associated technical documentation · Experience with V&V planning and requirements traceability; exposure to relevant standards (e.g. ARP4754, DEF STAN, MIL-STD, or equivalent) is an advantage · Solid understanding of at least one key effector subsystem domain – propulsion, structures, avionics, or guidance – with the breadth to work credibly across all of them · Structured, rigorous, and delivery-focused – able to drive technical decisions without getting lost in analysis · Fluent in English; German is an advantage Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Structural Dynamics Engineer
description: The Destinus engineering team is seeking an Aeroelastic/Structural Dynamics Engineer to lead structural dynamic and aeroelastic simulation activities across our vehicle programmes, from model setup through test correlation. The ideal candidate bridges analysis and test – ensuring dynamic behaviour is accurately predicted, verified, and substantiated against experimental data. What You’ll Do · Set up, execute, and post-process structural dynamics and aeroelastic simulations · Create and maintain Global Finite Element Models (GFEM) representing vehicle-level dynamic behaviour, ensuring consistency and traceability with detailed local FE models · Support structural dynamic qualification and verification of components, subsystems, and full vehicle assemblies · Define, document, and oversee execution of vibration, modal survey, and ground vibration test (GVT) campaigns · Correlate simulation predictions against experimental test data; interpret and communicate results clearly · Prepare technical reports, analysis documentation, and design justification packages Requirements What You’ll Need · Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field · 3–5 years of industry experience in structural dynamics, aeroelasticity, or vibration engineering · Proficiency with FEA packages: NASTRAN (Femap or equivalent), Abaqus, or Optistruct – for modal, transient, frequency response, and/or random vibration analysis · Demonstrated experience defining and executing vibration and dynamic test plans · Strong ability to correlate experimental test data against simulation predictions · Solid grounding in structural dynamics fundamentals: SDOF/MDOF systems, modal analysis, damping, and forced response Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Structural Design Engineer
description: The Destinus engineering team is seeking a Structural Design Engineer to own the CAD design of aeronautical structures from concept through production support. title: Stress Engineer - Non-linear & Propellants
description: The Destinus engineering team is seeking a Stress Engineer to support structural sizing and simulation with a focus on non-linear and thermomechanical analysis of solid rocket motor structures. A core part of this role is the structural simulation of propellant grains, liner bonds, thermal protection systems (TPS), and propellant–liner–casing interfaces – combining FEA with material characterization and test correlation to build substantiated models of energetic material assemblies. What You’ll Do · Conduct stress analysis using both classical hand-calculation methods and FEA – linear and non-linear, static and dynamic · Simulate solid rocket motor structures: propellant grain stress and strain fields, bond integrity at propellant–liner and liner–casing interfaces, TPS thermomechanical response, and igniter/nozzle attachment loads · Conduct non-linear simulations covering geometric non-linearity, material non-linearity (plasticity, hyperelasticity for propellant and elastomeric materials), and contact mechanics · Perform thermomechanical analysis across metallic, composite, bonded, and polymeric structures under thermal cycling and operational loads · Support experimental characterisation of propellant, liner, and bonded joint materials; feed test results (lap shear, peel, tensile, and DMA data) into material models and allowables · Correlate FE predictions against strain gauge, load, and thermal test data; validate and update models accordingly · Prepare stress reports, margin-of-safety calculations, and design justification documentation Requirements What You’ll Need · Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field · 3–5 years of industry experience in stress analysis of aerospace or mechanical structures · Proficiency with FEA packages: NASTRAN (Femap or equivalent), Abaqus, or Optistruct/HyperWorks for both linear and non-linear analysis · Strong classical stress analysis skills: beam theory, buckling, fastener and joint analysis, margin-of-safety calculations · Experience with non-linear material modelling – plasticity, hyperelasticity, or viscoelasticity; familiarity with propellant or elastomeric material constitutive models is a strong advantage · Experience with thermomechanical or thermal-structural analysis · Experience correlating FE predictions with experimental test data · Background in solid rocket motor, propulsion, or energetic structures is a strong advantage · Fluent in English; title: Flight Physics & Performance Engineer
description: We are looking for a highly capable Flight Physics & Performance Engineer to support the development, implementation, and validation of high-fidelity simulation environments for missile system performance analysis. In this role, you will design and maintain 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) simulation frameworks, implement flight physics and guidance models, and ensure simulation tools are robust, scalable, and aligned with system requirements. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to enable accurate performance predictions and support broader system design activities. This position is ideal for an engineer with strong analytical skills, hands-on experience in simulation toolchains, and a passion for advancing the modelling capabilities behind next-generation missile systems. Responsibilities · Develop, maintain, and extend 6-DoF simulation environments for missile performance assessment, system trade studies, and design validation. · Implement and refine flight physics models, including aerodynamics, propulsion behavior, actuator dynamics, sensor models, and environmental effects. · Build and integrate simulation tools and analysis utilities to support SIL, CIL, and HIL test configurations. · Define, decompose, and manage system and simulation requirements using DOORS NG or similar systems engineering tools. · Generate clear, structured, and technically rigorous documentation, covering modelling assumptions, equations of motion, validation results, and verification. · Produce and execute test cases for requirement verification across multiple simulation levels (SIL, CIL, HIL). · Work cross-functionally with Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC), Systems Engineering, Software, and Flight Dynamics teams to ensure model fidelity and alignment with system needs. · Participate in design and technical reviews, presenting simulation methodologies, performance outcomes, and model limitations. · Support algorithm development teams by providing simulation environments, interfaces, and validation scenarios. · Actively contribute to continuous improvement of internal simulation capabilities, toolchains, and workflows. · Represent the simulation domain in external collaborations, technical meetings, or strategic advisory groups when required. Requirements · Proven experience developing and managing 6-DoF simulations for aerospace or missile systems. · Strong understanding of flight mechanics, aerodynamics, propulsion models, rigid-body dynamics, and related numerical methods. · Hands-on experience with simulation tool development, including model integration, scenario generation, and test automation. · Proven coding experience preferred: Python, C/C++, Rust. · Experience with SIL, CIL, and HIL simulations and verification processes. · Strong technical writing skills and experience in producing advanced engineering documentation. · Proficiency with MATLAB/Simulink or equivalent modelling environments; experience with MathWorks tools is highly valued. · Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams and communicate complex technical topics clearly. · Proactive attitude, good problem-solving skills, and willingness to take ownership of simulation tasks and toolchain development. MSc in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related fields. · Fluency in English is a must. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Associate Director/ Director FP&A EMEA
description: Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need. As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at ScholarRock.com and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn. Summary of Position: Reporting to the VP, Finance EMEA, the Associate Director/ Director, FP&A will support Scholar Rock’s EMEA organization. The successful candidate will bring a proven track record of planning and delivering against financial objectives in close partnership with cross-functional stakeholders. In this role, they will serve as a strategic partner in framing, evaluating, and driving decisions to maximize value creation. Success will require clear communication, strong organization, and a collaborative mindset. This position offers an opportunity to help build a critical cross-functional capability within a growing, evolving, multi-product candidate biotechnology company. Position Responsibilities Serve as the primary finance partner for the EMEA scope across revenue and OPEX planning. Support FP&A activities including budgeting and forecasting, long-range planning, scenario modeling, and financial analysis for strategic initiatives. Build and maintain patient and revenue models, ensuring appropriate underlying assumptions for direct and partner markets. Partner with EMEA Accounting on month-end and quarter-end close activities, quarterly schedules, procure-to-pay processes, and support for external reporting and audit inquiries. Deliver timely monthly budget-to-actual analyses, including variance analysis and management reporting. Drive continuous improvement of FP&A processes to increase efficiency while maintaining flexibility to meet evolving business needs. Develop and deliver training and change-management support to drive adoption of new FP&A tools, systems, and ways of working across the organization. Support ad hoc strategic initiatives as business needs arise, including business development analyses, partner support, portfolio prioritization, and financing strategies. Candidate Requirements Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of progressive finance experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry. Advanced degree in science and/or business preferred. Experience partnering with Commercial and/or Medical teams in a cross-functional environment. Excellent presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization. Strong partnering and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, actionable insights. Advanced Excel skills and the ability to conduct complex analyses to support key decisions. Solid understanding of fundamental accounting principles. Understanding of the drug development process from early research through product launch. Strong organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. Experience with Adaptive Insights and/or SAP is an asset. We already have a high-potential strategy in place—your mission is to take the reins, execute it flawlessly, adapt it when necessary, and expand upon it wherever possible. Given the strategic importance of this initiative to Satispay, you will work with a high degree of autonomy and have direct, frequent touchpoints with the Satispay founding team to align on execution, team scaling, and long-term vision. Here’s what that looks like in practice: Hire & Build Your Team: Identify talent needs, recruit, and structure a dedicated, high-performing cross-functional team from the ground up to bring Satispay's crypto vertical to life. Execution & Strategic Evolution: Take ownership of our existing crypto roadmap. Drive its execution to deliver immediate impact, while continuously evaluating the market to make necessary adjustments and expand our offerings when new opportunities arise. Executive Collaboration: Partner directly with the founders and C-level executives to ensure the crypto rollout continuously aligns with the company's ultimate mission to simplify everyday finance. Product Development: Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of our crypto products—from infrastructure setup and go-to-market strategy to launch and continuous optimization. Regulatory Navigation: Work in lockstep with the Compliance and Legal teams to ensure all products align perfectly with evolving European regulations (such as MiCA) and safeguarding standards. title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy, Intern
description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware. The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one. This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes. What You'll Work On Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities. Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather. Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer. Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts. Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions. Apply solid engineering practices: code review, version control, reproducible experiments and clear documentation. Who We're Looking For We're looking for a strong robotics student who wants to see their work run on real robots, not only in simulation. Your Background Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD, or completed a Master's degree within the last year, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. Demonstrated depth in at least one of perception, localisation and state estimation, or motion planning and navigation, through a thesis, research or a substantial project. Strong coding skills in Python. Hands-on experience with ROS 2. Comfortable using Linux, Docker and Git in your workflows. Nice to Have Experience working with physical robots, ideally mobile or legged. Experience with lidar or camera processing, SLAM, or sensor fusion. Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo or MuJoCo. Publications or competition results in robotics (ICRA, IROS, RSS, CoRL). What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow. Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team. Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously. title: Head of Hardware
description: Accelerating embodied AGI. The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century. MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data. We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries. Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors. You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them. This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage. What You Will Do Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why. Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree. Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room. Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets. Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy. Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability. Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured. Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result. Requirements You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale. Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today. You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer. You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took. A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly. Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification. Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice. High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before. Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care. Nice to Have Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé. Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization. Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures. Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time. Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong. Open-source hardware or firmware contributions. Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits: Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it. Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it. Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them. Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes. This is for you if: You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec. You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one. You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do. This is not for you if: You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. You would forward output you cannot explain. "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer. How We Hire We read every application and reply within five working days. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem. Then a decision, usually within a few days. Pay Transparency Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting. What We Offer Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter. Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval. A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage. Free food and drinks in the office. Equal Opportunity MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. The Head of Credit Risk Oversight is a senior risk leadership role in the Second Line of Defence (2nd LoD), shaping how Monzo Bank Europe lends as it scales across the continent. You'll join early enough to set the standard, and stay to see it grow with the portfolio. Roles like this don't come along often.</p> <p>You'll lead the oversight of Monzo Bank Europe’s whole lending business. That means driving our Credit Risk Framework, defining the risk appetite, challenging and shaping our credit strategy, and overseeing how the business executes it within that appetite, right across the credit lifecycle. You'll spot the risks inthe portfolio before they show up in the numbers, so Monzo Bank Europe can grow fast and keep growing.</p> <p>You'll also lead our credit risk analytics and measurement. You'll direct the development of our IFRS 9 expected credit loss models, make sure our impairment provisions hold up, and turn portfolio data into insight the business acts on. You'll do that with modern methods and technology, including artificial intelligence, and set the standard for how we use and control them.</p> <p>This role reports to the Director of Credit Risk, Monzo Bank Europe.</p> <p><em>The role you are applying for is a Controlled Function (CF-2) within the meaning of the Central Bank Reform Act, 2010. For this role, appointment will be conditional on Monzo being fully satisfied that the appointee meets the requirements as set out in the Fitness and Probity Standards 2018 issued by the Central Bank of Ireland. As a CF, the role holder will be subject to Conduct Standards under the Central Bank of Ireland Individual Accountability Framework and will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure that the relevant conduct standards are met.</em></p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by...</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong> Credit Risk Framework and Appetite</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Developing, implementing and continuously improving our Credit Risk Framework in Europe, keeping it aligned to the entity's strategy.</li> <li>Formulating and overseeing the Credit Risk Appetite Statement and its limit structure, so lending growth stays inside agreed boundaries.</li> <li>Turning appetite into practical limits, triggers and escalation paths, and overseeing how the First Line of Defence (1st LoD) puts them into practice.</li> <li>Embedding group-wide credit risk frameworks locally, with clear escalation between global standards and local policy.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> 2nd LoD oversight of credit risk activities</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Giving independent oversight and challenge across credit policy, underwriting and credit decisioning strategies, affordability, pricing, and collections and recovery.</li> <li>Issuing formal 2nd LoD opinions on new products, policy and strategy changes, and material lending decisions.</li> <li>Reviewing portfolio asset quality regularly, including performance trends, vintage analysis and emerging pockets of risk.</li> <li>Overseeing the adequacy assessment of IFRS 9 impairment provisions, and giving a clear 2nd LoD view on whether provisions are appropriate.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Credit risk measurement</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Leading the measurement of our credit risk end to end, from data and methodology through to the loss estimates we report.</li> <li>Owning the development and maintenance of the IFRS 9 expected credit loss models, including the PD, LGD, EAD and forward-looking information (FLI) inputs behind them.</li> <li>Setting the methodology for staging, significant increase in credit risk, macroeconomic scenarios and post-model adjustments.</li> <li>Keeping model documentation and evidence in good shape, and closing validation findings on time.</li> <li>Bringing advanced techniques and artificial intelligence into how we build and run these models, with the controls and transparency that come with them.</li> <li>Supplying credit risk parameters and expert input to capital, stress testing and financial planning work.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Monitoring, early warning and MI</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Building credit risk monitoring and early warning processes that spot problems early.</li> <li>Delivering high quality, timely credit risk management information and insight to senior internal and external stakeholders.</li> <li>Making the numbers tell a clear story, so people can make decisions quickly and confidently.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Committee governance and independent challenge</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Acting as Secretariat and Deputy Chair of the Credit Risk Oversight Committee, shaping agendas, tracking actions, and presenting 2nd LoD reports and opinions.</li> <li>Escalating credit risk appetite breaches and material risks promptly to the Executive Risk Committee and the Board Risk Committee.</li> <li>Giving clear, evidence-based challenge to 1st LoD credit, analytics and product teams, and to accountable executives.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Regulatory compliance and engagement</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Making sure credit risk management meets the legal and regulatory requirements of the markets we operate in, including Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) requirements, Irish and European Union law, and European Banking Authority (EBA) and European Central Bank (ECB) guidelines.</li> <li>Leading the 2nd LoD assessment of changing and new credit regulation.</li> <li>Supporting regulatory reporting and engagement, and supporting the Director of Credit Risk on executing their PCF-22 obligations.</li> <li>Acting as a key point of contact for the CBI, internal audit and external auditors on credit risk matters.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Leadership and stakeholder management</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Building the credit risk oversight function from the ground up. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. FinCrime, AML/ CTF vision and strategy.</li> <li>Helping to build and oversee solutions with technology at the heart of our screening, onboarding and transaction monitoring mitigation strategies to cover the various typologies using automated alerts.</li> <li>Supporting the Director of FinCrime, Fraud and Disputes operations with producing Committee packs.</li> <li>Supporting and managing the oversight of change implementation, making prioritisation calls of those initiatives. </li> <li>Working closely with the second line of defence and our Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) to complete assurance activity, identification and remediation of any actions. </li> <li>Collaborating across the company to remove roadblocks and solve complex challenges relating to Monzo's EU and high performance. </li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You excel at leveraging robust data insights and analytics to drive strategic decision-making.</li> success.</li> <li>You have previous experience leading and managing FinCrime operations in payments or banking.</li> <li>You enjoy partnering with 3rd party vendors, data scientists, and second line of defence (2LOD) to proactively mitigate and respond to existing and emerging fraud trends.</li> <li>You understand the Financial crime,  money mulling risks of the various products and services operating in the fintech space.</li> <li>You champion the use of automated processes to find more efficient ways of working.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💶 A salary range of €76,500 - €95,500 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance</p> <p>📍This role will have a hybrid working model, based in our Dublin office 3 days a week. You will also travel to Monzo’s head office in London from time to time</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team</p> <p>🏝 Annual Leave - 34 days including public holidays (24 holiday days + 10 public holidays)</p> <p>📚€1,200 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences</p> <p>🏥 Private healthcare scheme</p> <p>💰Pension scheme: the minimum contribution is 4% and Monzo matches any additional contributions that you make up to a maximum of 6%</p> <p>💛 Wellbeing benefits: financial education, women’s and men’s health support, mental health benefits, including coaching and counselling</p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has 3 key steps</strong></p> <ol> <li>An introductory video call with a member of the Monzo Recruitment team</li> <li>An initial video call with the hiring manager</li> <li>A series of role specific, behavioural & leadership principles interviews</li> </ol> <p>This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!
